## November 27 — Private proof budgets and the first global parameter lookup

The 123 private SMT checks reached during early proofs on four complete verifiers returned 50 SAT, 16 UNSAT and 57 unknown. Every unknown reported incomplete quantifiers. **Zero checks exhausted their allowance.** The observer recorded resource steps immediately before and after the child check, the effective limit, the actual return value and unknown reason. Three GC-off runs reproduced each input's per-plan sequence and reference transcript. The table includes checks inside successful and unsuccessful early attempts. Other private strategies can finish without calling this solver.

| Input | SAT / unknown / UNSAT | SAT instructions (M) | Unknown instructions (M) | UNSAT instructions (M) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Hybrid reliable broadcast | 10 / 30 / 8 | 15.57 | 85.24 | 27.46 |
| test/flash2 | 21 / 11 / 2 | 34.10 | 60.80 | 7.51 |
| CAV examp5 | 15 / 12 / 4 | 34.02 | 61.25 | 33.01 |
| POPL18 Ticket | 4 / 4 / 2 | 4.45 | 11.78 | 5.83 |

We tested reducing the 6,000-step definition-plan allowance to 256 or 512. All three releases matched all 228 reference transcripts. Across seven normal-GC pairs on each of six inputs, 256 saved 0.60–1.77% of whole-verifier instructions. Nine follow-up triples on outliers exposed a genuine lost proof. On CAV examp1 the original solver had used 220 steps by the time search started and finished UNSAT at step 526. The 256-step variant stopped at step 257, then spent a further 1.46M instructions on a satisfiable secondary plan and sent the goal to the concrete solver. The 256 and 512 variants increased complete examp1 instructions by 3.47% and 3.57%. Both reproduced the Raft and Apple proof transcripts in three rotations. Keep the original allowance. A blanket reduction penalizes this cheap successful proof.

### Why private solver construction reads the whole parameter catalog

During failed early attempts, the cold solver factory spent 21.48M instructions constructing SMT parameters on hybrid, 27.95M on test/flash2 and 22.64M on examp5. A finer probe measured **20.01M, 26.61M and 21.63M** in the global `auto_config` read inside parameter updates during construction. These numbers come from separate instrumented builds. The first default lookup invokes the catalog dispatcher, which populates descriptors for the global options and 19 modules. A private manager can pay this cost even when it only needs the default of one option. The C++ source uses process-wide global parameters. g3 gives the private context its own registry.

A diagnostic build returned the built-in default on that first lookup in the private prover when the option was absent and its catalog was still unregistered. Seven paired release runs per input saved 0.13–1.87% of instructions on six verifiers. The experiment changes when descriptor registration, symbol interning and potential allocation failures occur. It remains an estimate of the opportunity. A production design would need to preserve user-configured defaults and observable initialization behavior. The existing complete-catalog metadata and fault-injection tests provide controls.

### Parameter descriptor dictionary

Commit `2214ce42a` improves an ordinary lookup without changing when g3 registers descriptors. For names in the same manager, the old hash put the varying symbol ID in the high 32 bits. The dictionary selects its initial bucket with a low-bit mask, so every ordinary name started in the same bucket at the measured sizes. Its probing sequence eventually used the high bits and found the correct name. Mixing the symbol ID and tag before indexing distributes the starting positions. Keys still use full symbol equality, incoming keys still undergo owner validation, and the insertion-ordered dictionary preserves iteration order.

| Benchmark | Original | New hash |
|---|---:|---:|
| Lookup among 32 names | 51.54 ns | 40.50 ns |
| Lookup among 512 names | 53.50 ns | 41.44 ns |
| Lookup among 4,096 names | 59.04 ns | 42.85 ns |
| First global default lookup, including registry creation and close | 198.03 µs | 186.88 µs |

Each entry is the median of nine alternating runs pinned to one CPU. The first three used 500,000 lookups per sample, with zero allocations. The last used 60 fresh registries sharing a warm symbol manager and catalog. Each used 421 allocations per operation on both builds. A separate insertion prototype removed a repeated symbol check on the freshly interned path. First lookup went from 181.15 to 175.95 µs in that series. It is archived pending end-to-end and lifetime validation.

The release passed the parameter, API and SMT suites, the checked/debug/trace parameter suite and the 228-input verifier transcript screen. Three complete rotations also matched Raft, Apple rfn2 and dramc_nb2. Their median paired instruction changes were −0.13%, +0.26% and +0.06%. In five rotated original/release/native triples, median paired whole-verifier instructions changed by −0.62% to +0.87% across six inputs. On hybrid the released g3 took 1,125 ms versus 828 ms for linked Z3. On Ticket it took 425 ms versus 234 ms. The lookup speedup is repeatable in the component benchmark. The complete verifier measurements still leave a substantial gap. ### November 27 — Models of selected premises and a missed Flash instance

We captured the exact 123 private solver inputs from hybrid reliable broadcast, test/flash2, CAV examp5 and POPL18 Ticket. The capture reproduced every original private answer and the four complete verifier transcripts. A fresh native simple solver linked with GoIvy's Z3 archive, with macro finding enabled and MBQI disabled, gave **the same 123 answers as g3**. With model-based quantifier instantiation (MBQI) enabled, native classified 56 of the 57 unknowns as SAT and one as UNSAT. Thus most of this search was spent trying to refute satisfiable *selected premises*. The full verification problems also contain assertions the private solver omitted.

| Input | Private unknowns | SAT with singleton user sorts | SAT with at most two elements per user sort | Final g3 filter recognizes (unknown / already SAT) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Hybrid broadcast | 30 | 28 | 30 | 18 / 2 |
| test/flash2 | 11 | 6 | 9 | 2 / 7 |
| CAV examp5 | 12 | 2 | 12 | 0 / 2 |
| POPL18 Ticket | 4 | 1 | 4 | 1 / 4 |

Flash private check 11 was the one missed refutation. Deletion reduced it to assertions 5, 7, 8 and 9. Adding one instance of assertion 5 at the existing constants `@X, @Y, @Z` to the original input allowed native E-matching alone to prove UNSAT. Adding only the instance of assertion 7 did not. The two instances plus the two ground assertions were UNSAT, and deleting either instance made the ground problem SAT. This supports investigating which existing terms or partial matches fail to trigger assertion 5. Turning on g3 MBQI across the private search increased complete instructions on five of six workloads by 1.15–6.69% in seven pairs. We retained the existing search configuration.

**The retained change, `f9070483c`, checks up to 64 constant predicate interpretations before starting a private refutation.** Each bit tracks one common interpretation across all selected formulas. A quantified body is accepted only when its value holds uniformly. Equality may use a singleton user domain after checking that the expressions contain only basic and uninterpreted applications. This guard excludes distinguished model-value constants. Unknown expressions, excessive traversal, and a missing certificate fall through to the existing private check. Finding a witness declines that one refutation strategy. The full solver remains responsible for the original proof. Diagnostic and failure-injection paths retain their previous behavior. [Implementation](api/api_private_premise_model.go) · [Regressions and benchmark](api/api_private_premise_model_test.go)

A shadow build left all solver calls enabled and recorded the independent filter result. All 36 selections it recognized had a singleton-domain SAT answer from native. The 21 previously unknown checks alone had cost 52.91M retired instructions inside their private checks, excluding setup. The benchmark of a reusable solver with a satisfiable universal subset dropped from a median of 593 µs, 331 KB and 1,350 allocations to 248 ns and zero allocations. This benchmark isolates the avoided private call. The caller still pays to select premises and check the full problem.

Nine rotated baseline/release/native runs used pinned CPU 12, normal GC, the same frontend and the retained PGO profile. The instruction changes below are medians of within-round release/baseline differences. The elapsed columns are separate medians. The warm machine also ran other studies during portions of this panel.

| Complete GoIvy input | g3 instruction change | Released g3 ms | Linked Z3 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Hybrid broadcast | −1.73% | 1,088 | 826 |
| test/flash2 | −1.50% | 885 | 875 |
| CAV examp5 | +0.20% | 510 | 490 |
| CAV examp1 | −0.23% | 77 | 100 |
| POPL18 Ticket | −2.26% | 452 | 242 |
| test/skolem1 | −20.41% | 23.5 | 30.4 |
| examples/liveness/ticket | −5.11% | 243 | 208 |

All 228 complete verifier transcripts and exit statuses matched their native references. Three paired rotations of ordinary Raft, Apple rfn2 and dramc_nb2 also matched. Across 101 alternating same-binary pairs its median difference was −0.32%. Another 51 pairs with the switch disabled on both sides differed by +0.01%. Toy consensus provides no reproducible evidence of work saved by the filter. POPL18 Ticket remains the largest elapsed ratio in the eight-input panel. The earlier matched profile attributed 995M excess instructions to its checks and 56M to batch 4 goal 55 after Push. That concrete operation is a larger target than the remaining private unknowns. [Ticket phase and obligation profiles](#november-27--where-the-four-ticket-verifiers-spend-their-instructions)

On dramc_nb2 the first panel showed +9.45% elapsed despite almost unchanged instruction counts. Three further pairs after concurrent builds finished gave -0.10% instructions and -2.43% elapsed. The two panels do not establish a wall-time improvement on this isolate. [Captured SMT-LIB inputs, native replay, prototype sources, benchmark drivers and raw results](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-private-quantifier-models.tar.xz)

### November 27 — Why the complete POPL18 Ticket solver costs more

The previous 56M-instruction deficit for batch 4 goal 55 came from a historical release. We repeated the measurement from commit `009f2e291` in the complete GoIvy process, with the same frontend and linked Z3 archive. Nine alternating pairs counted user instructions on the solver thread strictly between entry to and return from the check, after Push and Assert. Eleven alternating sampling pairs attributed instructions only to the target thread and check interval. The PGO build inlines g3's instance dispatcher and some theory-rewriter calls, so the classification also recognizes the queue callback and underlying rewriter engine. Three separate event-counting pairs measured how each candidate finished. Every captured verifier exit code and both output streams matched the native reference.

| Ticket batch/goal | Median check instructions, g3 / Z3 (M) | Candidates reaching the instance checker, g3 / Z3 | Lemmas asserted, g3 / Z3 | Sampled assertion instructions per asserted lemma, g3 / Z3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4/55 | 81.48 / 13.94 | 2,654 / 887 | 725 / 356 | 25,188 / 5,014 |
| 4/56 | 34.37 / 13.34 | 964 / 918 | 325 / 329 | 17,757 / 5,003 |
| 5/55 | 56.26 / 25.35 | 1,434 / 2,096 | 530 / 534 | 24,625 / 4,637 |
| 5/56 | 49.37 / 20.48 | 1,557 / 1,660 | 497 / 488 | 18,513 / 5,072 |

On 4/55, g3 discarded 1,929 candidates as already satisfied, compared with 531 for Z3. All remaining candidates were asserted. Neither engine rewrote any to true. G3 does more search *and* pays more for each lemma on this goal. In contrast, g3 considers fewer candidates on 5/55 and asserts four fewer lemmas. That sibling isolates the higher price of a roughly matched amount of solver work. The per-lemma column divides estimated inclusive assertion instructions by independently counted lemmas. Clause shapes, object counts per lemma and GC can differ. On 4/55, disjoint sampled excesses include 16.48M in assertion, 9.61M in rewriting, 9.61M in E-matching, and 5.21M in substitution.

Five further pairs instrumented operations inside the fresh formula calls made by lemma assertion. GC was disabled for these per-operation measurements. The inner probes calibrate adjacent reads of a hardware counter. Their enclosing intervals include the cost of nested probes.

| Operation inside fresh operands | 4/56 calls g3 / Z3 | 4/56 instructions/call g3 / Z3 | 5/55 calls g3 / Z3 | 5/55 instructions/call g3 / Z3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Create enode | 355 / 362 | 2,526 / 712 | 621 / 653 | 2,529 / 747 |
| Create Boolean variable | 391 / 395 | 692 / 245 | 684 / 728 | 703 / 279 |
| Emit gate clause | 155 / 142 | 1,322 / 360 | 266 / 285 | 1,301 / 370 |

The matched siblings make enode construction a better target than adjusting queue order across workloads. On 5/55 g3 creates fewer enodes and still spends about 3.5× the instructions per creation. Boolean-variable construction and gate-clause emission also show a persistent per-call gap. These intervals nest, so adding their excesses would overstate the recoverable cost.

**Memory and GC.** On 4/55, seven paired heap observations measured about 1.38 MB and 15,953 Go allocations before the operand-storage change. A separate differential allocation profile, excluding the profiler's own encoding stacks, attributed about 186 KiB to enode creation, 181 KiB to fingerprints and 124 KiB to finishing quantifier lemmas. These are allocation samples. Exact counts use differences in runtime allocation counters. GC-off check medians were 69.62M / 13.94M instructions on 4/55 and 49.89M / 25.35M on 5/55. Turning off GC across complete Ticket took g3 from 2.87B to 2.38B instructions but raised peak RSS from 46 to 129 MiB. Median elapsed was 419 versus 421 ms. Z3 went from 1.46B to 1.33B instructions, including its Go frontend. Tuning process-wide GC would leave most of the instruction deficit and would affect every worker.

**Seven queue and watch trials.** Nine rotated triples compared the original policy with a stable low-cost-first queue and reverse insertion order. Low-cost-first saved 2.48% of complete POPL18 instructions but cost 2.66% on liveness Ticket and 5.81% on Flash. Reverse order cost 36.56% on ARM. Five further rotations compared eager thresholds of zero and two and a threshold of two restricted to batches of at least 16 candidates. The batch restriction saved 3.46% on POPL18 and 5.05% on liveness Ticket but cost 24.46% on ARM. A zero threshold nearly doubled POPL18 instructions. Reusing a positive operand's sign during watch registration and coallocating children for disjunctions up to width eight each moved complete instructions by less than 1% on all five inputs. All seven alternatives reproduced the reference transcripts. Production retains its original scheduling and watch policies.

**Reuse the operand slice during lemma construction.** `a656e6f29` lends one buffer per builder to the call assembling the guard and disjuncts. A borrowed slice becomes available again after the call finishes, including nested assertions. The builder retains up to 32 handles. On 4/55 this removed **718 allocations and about 60 KB**. Across all four checks, allocations fell by 4.36–4.56%, bytes by 4.38–5.69%, and GC-off check instructions by 0.12–0.20%. The four-disjunct benchmark fell from 161 to 81 B/op, two allocations to one, and 1,111 to 1,081 ns/op over eleven alternating pairs. Whole-verifier instructions changed by −1.63% on POPL18, +0.30% on liveness Ticket, effectively zero on hybrid, +0.95% on ARM and −0.28% on Flash. We retained this change for the reproducible allocation and local instruction reduction. [Benchmark and nested operand regression](smtcore/smt_qi_lemma_benchmark_test.go)

**Read prepared-body reference counts only where they control memoization.** Sampling found repeated arena reference-count reads during checks of candidate bindings. The syntax compiler has already assigned memo slots to subexpressions that may be revisited. `e977d5f08` validates the root once, uses its ownership of the immutable body, and skips the count read for nodes with no slot. Nodes with a slot retain the existing sharing rule. The generation check caught a distinction between release-build reference-count lookup and handle validation. An explicit regression drops the prepared body's last reference and checks the reported lifetime error. A diagnostic that always memoized eligible nodes ran faster in isolation, but broadened caching to expressions with one reference. The production change preserves the previous conditions for congruence and disequality lookups. [Checker and lifetime regression](smtcore/smt_checker_candidate_test.go)

Five rotating hardware-counter runs per method used 500,000 operations on the existing width-16 benchmark. For the last binding, the released checker used **10.72% fewer instructions** and the full queue path used **9.86% fewer**. The first binding, which succeeds with less work, saved only 0.20% and 0.12% respectively. Both methods still took zero allocations. In three instrumented full verifier runs, all four goals had exactly the baseline counts of satisfied candidates, true rewrites and asserted lemmas. Nine GC-off pairs put the combined production changes at −0.43% to −0.50% of instructions across the four complete check windows. [Prepared checker and queue benchmarks](smtcore/smt_quantifier_candidate_benchmark_test.go)

| Complete verifier | Combined g3 instruction change | Released g3 median ms | Linked Z3 median ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| POPL18 Ticket | −0.98% | 454 | 249 |
| Liveness Ticket | +0.07% | 249 | 210 |
| Hybrid broadcast | −0.13% | 1,150 | 858 |
| ARM rules | −0.33% | 461 | 338 |
| test/flash2 | −0.45% | 905 | 885 |

These nine rotated release/baseline/native triples used normal GC. The instruction percentages are medians of within-round differences and the times are separate medians. The 228 native reference transcripts and exit statuses matched. Three paired release rotations also matched ordinary Raft, Apple rfn2 and Apple dramc_nb2, with median instruction changes of −0.58%, −0.50% and −0.04%. Broader machine activity affected elapsed time during parts of the study. The improvements to allocation and per-binding checks are better established than a whole-verifier elapsed gain.

### How much of the Ticket gap could shared proofs recover?

We extended the fresh-operand counters to every reached check on three complete Ticket inputs, three runs per engine. At g3's own creation counts, replacing just the average per-enode price inside quantified assertions with native's measured price would save **30.89M instructions on POPL18, 26.28M on nested Ticket and 23.62M on Ticket L2S**. This includes only enodes reached by those instrumented formula calls. For POPL18 this is roughly 2% of the normal-GC whole-verifier gap. The expensive individual operation is real, but even bringing it to parity would leave most of that gap.

A separate experiment tested whether an earlier proof could discharge a later obligation with the same goal. We captured all native checks from the three complete verifier runs. For each input we expanded generated lets, split top-level conjunctions, and compared exact SMT terms and compatible declarations. We kept the 984 snapshots with a distinct base assertion and goal assertion. Ten L2S snapshots with additional top-level assertions were excluded. We kept user symbols and quantifier binder names intact. These bounds apply to this exact comparison, not to proofs under renaming or stronger logical implication.

For each later goal we formed its shared premises with every compatible earlier occurrence. Proving UNSAT on those premises and the unchanged goal establishes that a common proof is possible. A SAT model rules out a proof using any subset of those shared premises. Testing only inclusion-maximal intersections is sufficient. All 1,329 distinct native intersection checks returned SAT or UNSAT. We also extracted one unsatisfiable core per original input by assuming a fresh Boolean selector for each premise, checked each extracted core in a fresh untracked native solver, and simulated the chronological history. A hit uses an earlier learned core. Only misses add new cores. Zero POPL18 or nested Ticket hits were available by exact containment of an entire earlier premise set.

| Complete input | Checks analyzed / native checks | Later checks admitting a shared proof | Hits with one core learned per miss | g3 check instructions for hits (M) | All g3 check instructions (M) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| POPL18 Ticket | 284 / 284 | 71 | 63 | 286.56 | 1,584.18 |
| Nested Ticket | 413 / 413 | 148 | 146 | 43.76 | 1,421.46 |
| Ticket L2S | 287 / 297 | 79 | 74 | 36.80 | 1,392.31 |

The check weights are medians from five fresh full-verifier runs per engine with GC off. They assign zero direct check cost to obligations already discharged before that stage. The POPL18 upper bound with the best possible earlier shared premise set is 309.14M instructions. Its 63 practical core hits cover 286.56M, about nine times the projected enode saving on that input. POPL18 4/55 and 4/56 are both misses for the extracted cores. The benefit lies elsewhere in the same verifier. On nested Ticket, many hits already cost little with g3's current proof policy.

All 283 chronological hits also passed an independent check with the released g3 CLI on the target declarations, the earlier core and the target goal. All 63 POPL18 and 146 nested hits cross fresh solver batches. Of the 74 L2S hits, eight are within a batch. Any future implementation spanning batches needs verifier-job ownership and immutable evidence that remains valid across AST managers.

We then measured the end-to-end ceiling with a diagnostic that skips only those independently proved obligations when reached. The subsequent solver history evolves normally. All 54 complete verifier transcripts matched across nine rotated pairs per input. Median paired instruction savings were **13.47% on POPL18, 2.23% on nested Ticket and 1.01% on L2S**. Elapsed savings were 13.10%, 2.14% and 0.95%, respectively. POPL18 separate elapsed medians were 420 and 366 ms. These figures assume that learning and selecting a proof costs nothing.

Finally, a g3-only prototype learned cores chronologically. It replayed all 284 POPL18 obligations in batch order with a fresh incremental CLI process per batch. It used the same declaration set and premise order in each arm. The tracked arms guarded each premise with a Boolean selector and used check-sat-assuming. Only misses supplied new cores. Counts include CLI startup and parsing. Elapsed measurements also include preparing the batch in the driver. These replay timings have a different scope from the complete verifier timings above.

| POPL18 incremental CLI replay, three rotated runs | Checks solved | Checks reused | Median billion user instructions | Median elapsed ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Ordinary incremental checks | 284 | 0 | 3.115 | 643 |
| Track every premise | 284 | 0 | 6.734 | 1,099 |
| Track every miss and reuse earlier cores | 221 | 63 | 5.511 | 956 |

The g3 learner recovered 63 hits on every run. It still spent 77% more instructions than ordinary replay. We discarded the always-tracked prototype. The measured ceiling makes cheap dependency extraction or selective learning worth a bounded experiment. Its acquisition and lookup costs must fit inside the avoided checks on ordinary verification. Per-enode construction remains a smaller opportunity at the measured call counts. [Benchmark drivers, SMT inputs, controls and raw measurements](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-ticket-matched-siblings.tar.xz)

### November 27 — Selective core learning and joint proofs of sibling equalities

GoIvy commit `4b548dc4b` reduces **complete POPL18 Ticket from 419 to 386 ms** on the pinned verifier CPU. Linked Z3 took **238 ms**. Across seven rotated triples the median paired reduction was **6.13% of user instructions** and **8.46% of elapsed time**. The separate median instruction totals were 2.837B, 2.650B and 1.479B. The complete checker still takes about 1.62× as long as Z3. The change is in the GoIvy bridge that submits goals to g3. Each proof runs on the current solver and goroutine.

#### What selective core learning cost

We repeated the chronological POPL18 experiment with a plain incremental solver for ordinary misses and a separate incremental solver for the training subset of each batch. A compatible prior occurrence of the same goal had to exceed the threshold. The policy uses only earlier batches' median ordinary check costs. It has no access to future occurrences. Training checks answer the current obligation and supply a core for later batches. Each cache hit was verified by running g3 on the target signature, target goal and the earlier core alone. All 284 outcomes matched in each arm and rotation.

| Earlier cost threshold | Ordinary checks | Trained misses | Later hits | Ordinary check work covered by hits | Total replay instructions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| No learning | 284 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 3.087B |
| Any previous occurrence | 57 | 164 | 63 | 286.56M | 5.380B |
| ≥1M instructions | 167 | 79 | 38 | 245.61M | 4.657B |
| ≥5M instructions | 210 | 53 | 21 | 212.64M | 4.276B |
| ≥20M instructions | 264 | 18 | 2 | 56.20M | 3.871B |

Three rotations measured the complete CLI work including startup and parsing for each nonempty partition. Python matching costs and independent proof rechecks were outside those counters. The terminal identifier payload was only 1,632–6,064 bytes at four bytes per cached premise ID, excluding indexes, declarations and term storage. Even the most selective arm cost 25% more instructions than ordinary replay. We dropped this acquisition policy.

#### Which obligations benefit from a joint proof

Sibling checks share the same base. If the base plus the disjunction of several counterexample conditions is UNSAT, every sibling is proved. A SAT or unknown group requires ordinary individual checks to recover the first failing obligation and its model. This approach requires no core extraction or history across solvers.

On complete POPL18 an unrestricted group of up to 16 cut instructions by about 17%. The same policy raised Hybrid broadcast by 14%, examples/ivy/flash2 by 45%, and test/flash2 by 31%. Direct call windows with GC off explain the difference. Eighteen POPL18 groups saved 435M instructions against the corresponding individual windows. All 43 Hybrid groups also proved UNSAT, but their searches cost **996M additional instructions**. In examples/ivy/flash2, 36 of 140 grouped calls returned SAT and incurred individual retries. Triggering after a 0.3 or 1 ms individual check and running the private proof on later siblings first both retained substantial regressions.

Looking for a shared antecedent helped identify a better boundary. Allowing any identical antecedent still grouped 580 TLB spans. Together those grouped calls cost **25.10B** against **1.45B** in the corresponding individual check windows. On ARM just two groups cost 670M against 84M. Requiring a compound antecedent avoided those groups on both inputs. On POPL18 five groups of four with a shared compound guard cost **122M** against **342M** individually. They prove several guarded equalities at once. This measurement uses the factored-antecedent diagnostic with GC off.

The retained implementation recognizes runs of 3–16 concrete conjunction checkers whose equality or Boolean equivalence has the same compound antecedent. That shape determines when to try grouping. The actual proof disjoins the **complete translated conditions**, including constraints introduced by translation. It stops at assumptions, other checker types and different guards. After a SAT or unknown answer the temporary group scope is popped, and ordinary checks report failures in source order. The regression exercises satisfiable and unsatisfiable groups, the returned counterexample, scope restoration and a change of guard. Traced verification, explicit VC display and linked Z3 keep their individual checks. An experimental native build that did group these equalities changed POPL18 instructions by just −0.22%.

| Complete verifier | Paired g3 instruction change | Baseline g3 ms | Released g3 ms | Linked Z3 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| POPL18 Ticket | −6.13% | 419 | 386 | 238 |
| Nested Ticket | −1.37% | 439 | 438 | 327 |
| Liveness Ticket | −1.72% | 240 | 235 | 197 |
| Ticket L2S | +0.13% | 452 | 429 | 305 |
| Hybrid broadcast | −0.24% | 1,251 | 1,298 | 877 |
| ARM rules | +1.41% | 451 | 451 | 334 |
| test/flash2 | −0.38% | 911 | 908 | 885 |
| examples/ivy/flash2 | +0.38% | 679 | 677 | 629 |

Each row uses seven rotated triples with normal GC. Times are separate medians. Machine load varied, particularly for Hybrid. A second five-pair ARM measurement gave −0.05% instructions. Five complete inputs used the new path in an instrumented sweep of 228 verifiers. It proved 31 groups comprising 131 individual obligations across the three Ticket inputs using the path, POPL18 alternating bit, and test_liveness2. Nine repeated pairs on the last two gave −0.42% and **+1.09%** instructions, respectively. Every native reference transcript and exit status matched, including expected failures. Three additional pairs each on ordinary Raft, Apple rfn2 and dramc_nb2 also matched. Their instruction changes were +0.29%, +0.40% and −0.04%.

#### Where to look next on Hybrid broadcast

Across five full Hybrid runs per engine with GC off, native reached 839 individual checks and g3 reached 534. A check already discharged by the early proof path contributes zero to the individual check window. Summing per-goal median windows gave **3.665B g3 instructions versus 2.690B native**. Batch 31 accounts for 160.70M of the difference, followed by batches 33 and 34 at 103.85M and 96.54M. The two largest individual gaps are batch 31 goals 34 and 33 at 76.82M and 57.25M. Together these two account for about 14% of the net direct-check gap.

A second five-pair run measured other phases on the same target. G3 spent **1.124B against 543M on first pushes**, but only **242M against 1.143B** translating and asserting the base. Taken together those two phases favor g3 by 320M. Early private proofs cost 413M and eliminate many ordinary calls. Comparing first push or proof cost in isolation would misidentify the opportunity. Measure matched search events and normal-GC allocation on batches 31, 33 and 34 before changing preprocessing policy.

The normal-GC median instruction gap on Hybrid was **1.942B**. In seven complete paired runs with collection disabled for both frontends, the medians were **6.281B g3 and 5.324B native**, a gap of **0.956B**. About half of the normal-GC gap disappears under this diagnostic. Disabling GC changes allocation and memory behavior as well as collector work. It is unsuitable as a policy for thousands of independent solvers.

Across three normal-GC runs the g3 frontend and solver allocated a median **366.8 MB in 2.994M objects**, versus **98.8 MB in 1.320M Go objects** for the linked-native frontend. Native C++ heap allocations are outside the Go measurements. The median GC counts were 65 and 37. Sampled g3 allocation profiles charge 32.79 MiB cumulatively to ground projection problem construction, including 13.21 MiB directly in the projection reader. The bit compiler's interning method accounts for a further 9.58 MiB flat. Table-model compilation and the rewriter's cache-stack push each appear at about 131,000 sampled allocation objects. Sampled object estimates for small sites are noisy. Reuse per-solver projection scratch only after measuring how many sibling attempts repeat the same work and what memory survives batch close. Compare against eliminating model construction during failed private attempts, using proofs and models as controls. [Benchmark drivers, regressions, raw counter windows and whole-verifier results](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-selective-and-grouped-proofs.tar.xz)

## November 27 — Hybrid search volume, premise indexes and candidate-model operands

**G3 did less Boolean search and still paid more to assert quantifier instances.** On Hybrid broadcast, three complete runs per engine captured solver statistics immediately around goals 33 and 34 of batches 31, 33 and 34. The six check deltas totaled 4,489 quantifier instantiations in g3 versus 5,722 in linked Z3, 9,475 versus 10,527 decisions, 7,654 versus 9,781 Boolean variables created, and 61 versus 64 conflicts. Batch 31 goal 34 alone used 2,093 versus 2,597 instances and 4,249 versus 4,526 decisions, with a previously measured 77M excess g3 instructions. These are matched obligations with the same proof outcome. The engines can create different terms.

Seven instruction-sampled runs per engine placed 203M instructions under g3's `MaterializeAndInternalize` and 119M under Z3's per-entry `qi_queue::instantiate` across the six checks. Their assertion callees accounted for **106M versus 37M**. Inside the g3 assertion path, 55M went into Boolean formula internalization, 17M into marking relevance, 14M into adding the root clause and 8M into asserted-OR watches. Native split 15M into its formula-core entry, 3M into its separate equality entry and 6M into OR watches. These are sampled call stacks, with different inlining and entry boundaries.

A separate pair of instrumented builds then counted and priced operations **only while installing those instances**. Three GC-off replays per goal reproduced the counts and reference transcripts. The instruction figure is the sum of the six per-goal median costs divided by total calls. Hardware-counter reads were calibrated against empty reads. Some operations nest, so their totals cannot be added.

| Operation inside assertions | g3 calls | Z3 calls | g3 instructions/call | Z3 instructions/call |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Boolean variable creation | 7,607 | 9,723 | 734 | 271 |
| Enode creation | 6,003 | 7,911 | 2,737 | 739 |
| Congruence insertion inside enode creation | 6,003 | 7,911 | 506 | 148 |
| Gate construction | 1,690 | 1,943 | 9,456 | 3,171 |
| Gate clause insertion | 6,430 | 7,504 | 1,372 | 389 |

The g3 assertions also visited fewer root-OR operands (17,319 versus 22,499). At g3's measured volume, reaching Z3's per-call cost on enode creation would recover about 12.0M instructions on these goals. Reaching its cost for gate construction would recover about 10.6M. Gate clause insertion accounts for about 6.3M of that opportunity. These estimates hold the g3 search fixed. Gate and enode setup both merit comparison across workloads before changing layout.

**Parsed premise indexes.** Across 195 one-shot Hybrid projections, 163 used the cached parse. Those hits cloned indexes covering 63,058 premise nodes. Commit `4debdb162` reads the two immutable premise maps directly. Each goal owns the entries for its new terms and symbols. The original node and symbol order, work budget and cancellation checks remain observable in the sibling-goal regression. Seven rotating Apple obligation-71 benchmark runs put repeated projection at 886,130 → 722,418 B/op, 163 → 148 allocations/op and 1.002 → 0.980 ms/op. Fresh projection took 219 allocations in both builds.

Keeping the grounded applications as well saved more local work (163 → 133 allocations, 1.490 → 1.296 ms in its own paired experiment), but retained 1,672 versus 1,088 B per independent small solver. With 16 independent Apple contexts, retained heap rose from 434,268 to 592,632 B per solver. The shipped premise indexes measured 1,088 B and 437,684 B respectively, above the already loaded sources. Temporarily inserting and rolling back goal entries also reduced allocations, but showed no median projection-time advantage over its control. It would let a large transient goal grow the retained map.

**Candidate-model terms.** The Go model compiler allocated a separate operand slice for each application. Commit `1cb8c6aa2` appends operand IDs into private model-checker storage and stores a direct slice on each compiled term. The parent resolves its slice after recursive child compilation. Clearing the model drops buffers above 512 operand slots. Placing the unsigned variable/function/value index beside the operation reduces the amd64 term from 56 to 48 bytes. Full-width de Bruijn indices remain representable.

| Focused benchmark, median of nine | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ground enumeration | 3,537 ns | 3,479 ns |
| Allocated per enumeration | 288 B, 13 allocations | 232 B, 9 allocations |
| Retained per checker, 1,024 independent checkers | 2,624 B | 2,608 B |
| Binary function lookup, first row | 16.84 ns | 17.27 ns |
| Binary function lookup, last row | 37.72 ns | 36.07 ns |

Storing operand offsets instead of direct slices reduced the checker footprint further but increased the cost of accessing terms during evaluation. A separate prototype memoized single-binding subexpressions across tuples and debited their original work on cache hits. Complete Hybrid rose from 7.769B to 7.805B median instructions. Neither prototype shipped.

**Whole-process result.** With normal GC, the two shipped changes together took Hybrid from 366,825,832 to 361,983,800 allocated bytes and from 2,993,799 to 2,946,546 allocations (three runs per build). POPL18 Ticket saved 526,976 bytes and 482 allocations. On Hybrid, seven rotated complete runs retired 7.759B instructions before, 7.738B after and 5.823B with linked Z3. The allocation improvement is reproducible. These results do not establish a wall-time win. Timing and instruction counts are separate measurements, and validation jobs ran concurrently on this machine.

A second seven-round run after the Go suite finished put Hybrid at 1.112 s before, 1.119 s after and 0.858 s native. POPL18 Ticket took 392 ms before, 390 ms after and 238 ms native. The eight-case panel's median paired instruction changes ranged from a 1.30% saving on liveness Ticket to a 0.59% increase on ARM. All 228 reference exit codes and output streams matched. Three pairs each on ordinary Raft, Apple rfn2 and dramc_nb2 also matched, with median paired instruction changes of −0.44%, −0.14% and less than 0.01%, respectively. The full Go suite, focused checked/debug/trace tests and vet of the changed packages passed.

The source overlays, allocation census, paired benchmark rows, per-check counters, raw sampled stacks and transcript results are in the [experiment archive](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-hybrid-projection-and-model-tables.tar.xz). The checked-in worker benchmark runs with `go test ./api -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkQuantifiedPremiseWorkers$' -benchtime=2x`.

## November 27 — Complete Hybrid assertion costs and failed private proofs

On complete Hybrid, g3 installed 17,799 quantified instances and linked Z3 installed 28,065. We instrumented the same construction operations as in the six-check study across every physical check. The counts below cover work inside quantified assertions. Three complete GC-off runs per engine used a hardware counter on the solver thread, calibrated against adjacent empty reads. Each exit code and both output streams matched the native reference.

| Hybrid operation | g3 calls | Native calls | g3 instructions | Native instructions | Saving at g3 volume and native unit cost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Create enode | 25,000 | 39,371 | 68.1M | 30.0M | 49.1M |
| Construct gate | 7,217 | 8,689 | 69.6M | 28.6M | 45.9M |
| Install gate clause | 28,586 | 34,824 | 38.8M | 13.7M | 27.6M |
| Register Boolean variable | 31,161 | 46,919 | 22.9M | 13.4M | 14.0M |

Gate construction includes its gate clauses. Enode construction includes congruence insertion. These unit-cost estimates hold search volume fixed. Individually the two largest explain about 2.5% and 2.4% of the previously measured 1.94B normal-GC whole-process gap. The corresponding estimates for POPL18 Ticket are 30.9M and 16.8M instructions. A trial using fixed local operand buffers for short OR assertions and AND/OR gates increased Hybrid allocation by about 0.43 MB and its median paired instructions by 0.40%. The trial was discarded.

### When a private proof attempt returns to the general solver

A separate pair of hardware-counter reads around every private proof attempt includes cleanup. On Hybrid, 247 misses consumed **510.7M instructions** while 592 successful attempts took 253.8M. The ten most expensive misses alone cost 175.9M in the first round. POPL18's 125 misses consumed 164.9M, ARM's 61 consumed 84.9M, and liveness Ticket's 64 consumed 93.8M. These are three-run median totals with GC off. Among Hybrid misses, inclusive subpath measurements placed 165.6M under selection and checking of relevant premises, 146.5M under checking a Boolean projection, and 112.5M of the latter under SAT construction and search. Inclusive measurements overlap.

A diagnostic replay used the recorded obligation ordinals to decline expensive misses before entering the private strategies. Five rotated **normal-GC** runs compared this replay with its own instrumented control. Skipping the ten most expensive known misses saved 2.80% of complete Hybrid instructions and 5.02% on POPL18. Skipping all known misses saved 7.34% and 8.21%, respectively. Complete reference transcripts matched, but skipping all misses changed six later private outcomes on Hybrid and two on POPL18. These numbers include the effect of changed search history. The replay is a diagnostic with foreknowledge.

### A checked satisfying assignment avoids private SAT construction

After the unit reducer, a satisfiable Boolean projection cannot refute the original check. The ordinary solver still owns that check. Commit `6827279ff` tries positive decisions in two variable orders, propagates forced literals using occurrence lists and verifies the assignment against every remaining clause. Conflicts or incomplete attempts fall through to the existing SAT path subject to its resource limit. The implementation charges the private resource budget, polls for cancellation and bounds scratch at 256 variables and 512 clauses per attempt.

On 223 recorded residuals from eight verifiers, we compared constant assignments, monotone one-sign repair and implication propagation with deterministic decisions. On Hybrid, the all-false assignment satisfied eight residuals and forward monotone repair satisfied 38. Propagation in the two selected orders together satisfied 103. In the complete 228-input release census the implementation supplied **435 witnesses on 48 inputs**, out of 761 calls after reduction. Hybrid had 103 hits in 113 calls, POPL18 had 15 in 26, nested Ticket had 17 in 21 and automatic liveness-to-safety Ticket had 46 in 52. TLB had one hit in 106 calls. Across seven rotated pairs against the immediately preceding build, the witness check saved 2.06% of complete Hybrid instructions, 1.31% on POPL18 and 2.25% on automatic liveness-to-safety Ticket.

After the release, the same GC-off observer measured **112.30M → 10.23M instructions inside private SAT construction and search on Hybrid misses**, an elevenfold reduction in this path. The inclusive Boolean projection check fell from 146.21M to 49.47M; all private misses together fell from 510.73M to 402.63M. The remaining relevant-premise path measured 165.68M. Private plan calls, many nested under that path, measured 137.18M across all misses. Three independent per-check runs supply each median. The released results are in the archive's `post` directory.

In five extra transfer pairs, median instruction changes were −0.26% on low-hit TLB, −1.08% on POPL18 alternating bit, and −1.14%, +0.42%, −1.60% and −0.96% on CAV examp4, examp5, examp3 and examp2. Progress2, with one hit in nine calls, rose 0.29%. Small changes on individual holdouts vary in both directions.

The benchmark keeps actual forward-success, reverse-success and refuted Hybrid residuals. Each took zero allocations. A truth-table regression exhausts 1,023 subsets of ten small clauses and independently verifies the satisfiability of every positive result. Separate regressions cover cancellation, work exhaustion and preservation of the original clauses. [Witness benchmark and tests](api/internal/order/boolean_witness_test.go)

### Candidate-model and empty-map allocation

G3 eagerly built the value-to-context-term index at the start of every candidate check. The C++ `model_checker::get_term_from_ctx` populates it on first use. Commit `d2b5e26f1` borrows the generator during the check and builds the index on the first unrestricted witness. On Hybrid, none of 164 candidates needed the index (9,491 total roots). ARM needed it for nine of eleven candidates, a positive control for term recovery. In the 64-root benchmark, a candidate finishing without lookup took 8.57 µs and 9,560 allocated bytes with eager indexing, and 13.2 ns with zero allocations on demand. This benchmark isolates the unused index cost. [Candidate benchmark](smtcore/smt_model_checker_candidate_benchmark_test.go)

Commit `fa18b922b` defers the eight default AST object-map buckets until the first insertion. The logical capacity and iteration order match the eager map. The explicit-capacity constructor still provides the eager control. Constructing 1,024 empty maps went from 589,827 to 65,536 allocated bytes and from 2,048 to 1,024 allocations. An initial prototype panicked when erasing an absent pair from an empty copy. The regression covers this case, subsequent insertion and independent copy contents. [Map benchmark and regression](ast/ast_obj_map_capacity_test.go)

The rewriter census also found that 30,882 of 39,873 Hybrid activity caches closed without a successful insertion. The existing lazy entry storage already avoids their table allocation. The 311,880 probes returned 69,478 hits, including 4,941 that changed the term. A cache returning its input can still save an entire traversal. These counts alone do not justify removing it.

On POPL18 the corresponding figures were 100,102,120 → 97,923,616 bytes and 888,351 → 869,757 objects. Each of the three releases passed all 228 native transcript comparisons. ## November 27 — Models of the remaining relevant-premise subsets

Hybrid broadcast made 48 nonempty private attempts under relevant-premise selection. The existing filter declined 20. The narrow definition selector sent 14 subsets to a private solver, yielding eight SAT and six UNKNOWN. The rare-symbol selector sent another 14, yielding eight UNSAT proofs and six UNKNOWN. The wider definition selector produced no nonempty subset. No attempted check exhausted its step limit. Of the 20 calls where both selectors produced a subset, seven narrow subsets were contained in their rare-symbol sibling and 13 were incomparable. Replaying the exact solver inputs with linked Z3 and MBQI established that all 20 failed refutations were satisfiable. Fourteen admit a singleton interpretation of every user sort. Six require at least one domain of size two.

Across Hybrid, POPL18 Ticket, ARM rules and liveness Ticket, the observer captured 50 private solver invocations and 38 distinct SMT-LIB texts. No exact input repeated within its own proof batch. Caching these texts within a batch therefore offered zero hits. Narrow definition selection still produced private UNSAT proofs on the three controls.

### Search more constant-predicate interpretations before constructing a solver

The original evaluator searched all assignments to six predicates in one 64-bit word. The revised evaluator gives up to six further predicates a stable index and varies their truth values between words. A single bit must satisfy every selected assertion under the same interpretation. All words together share the original 512-node visit allowance. The existing check for interpreted terms still guards singleton-domain equality. This witness lets a speculative refutation decline. The original verification obligation still needs a proof.

Three prototypes ran in seven rotated normal-GC pairs on the same CPU. Seeding assignments from root literals found no additional Hybrid witnesses. Reusing combinations of the first six truth columns recognized six additional cases and saved 0.39% of complete Hybrid instructions. Enumerating independent truth values recognized 13 and saved 1.58%. The bounded release recognized the same 13 (four formerly SAT and nine formerly UNKNOWN) and one additional liveness Ticket subset. It retained all eight Hybrid private refutations.

Five 500-iteration samples put a captured Hybrid member subset at **663.48 µs → 2.34 µs**, **366,480 → 1,800 bytes**, and **1,700 → 5 allocations** per private plan. The small existing fixture measured 166.4 → 164.5 ns with zero allocations. The new positive regression failed on the previous implementation. Separate controls force a later block, contradict two roots, and distinguish interpreted model values. [Regression and benchmarks](api/api_private_premise_model_test.go)

The complete verifier comparison used seven rounds rotating the previous release, this change, and linked Z3 on one pinned CPU with normal GC. The instruction column is the median within-round change. Elapsed columns are separate medians. Concurrent machine load makes small elapsed changes uncertain.

| Complete workload | Paired g3 instruction change | Previous g3 | Revised g3 | Linked Z3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Hybrid broadcast | −1.79% | 1,086 ms | 1,058 ms | 839 ms |
| POPL18 Ticket | +0.92% | 389 ms | 390 ms | 240 ms |
| ARM rules | +0.95% | 460 ms | 463 ms | 338 ms |
| Liveness Ticket | −0.32% | 236 ms | 239 ms | 205 ms |

Three complete Hybrid allocation runs gave a median of **336,637,432 bytes and 2,801,148 objects**, down 11,012,776 bytes and 39,029 objects from the previous release. The CAV examp1_l2s holdout saved 4.81% of instructions. Ordinary examp1 and skolem1 changed by −0.21% and −0.03%. All 228 corpus inputs matched linked Z3 on exit status, stdout and stderr. Ordinary Raft and Apple rfn2 and dramc_nb2 also matched in each of three rotating pairs. Their paired instruction changes were −0.05%, −0.73% and +0.04%.

### How much more can two-element models recover?

A scratch evaluator tested independent random two-element function tables. It evaluates each supported quantified formula under every binding and intersects satisfying assignments across assertions. Linked Z3 independently checked the bounded inputs. On the twelve known cases requiring two elements, 4,096 trial interpretations found ten witnesses (four of six Hybrid, three of three POPL18, three of three liveness Ticket). A 64-interpretation sample found one. Widths use separately drawn deterministic tables, so they need not recognize nested sets of cases. Python timings exclude parsing and do not predict Go verifier speed.

Even eliminating all twelve private calls would recover at most their directly observed 48.07M, 22.43M and 28.41M instructions respectively, before paying for detection and allowing for later search changes. On Hybrid that is about 0.64% of the complete run. The larger remaining question is why Ticket generates extra instances on 4/55 and why both Ticket and Hybrid pay more per enode. [Captured subsets, oracle replay, prototype sources and per-run measurements](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-relevant-premise-models.tar.xz)

## November 27 — The first different Ticket offer and the price of changing order search

The comparison starts at g3 commit `2281f7a2e` with the guarded-sibling GoIvy frontend. Earlier reports counted 725 asserted lemmas on POPL18 Ticket 4/55. The current release asserts **531**, versus **356** for linked Z3. With ordinary checks on the preceding siblings, current g3 reproduces the native sequence of 45 signed decisions, 887 offers and 356 asserted lemmas. The comparison normalizes generated symbols consistently within each event kind and accounts for symmetric equality operands. It includes event interleaving.

With the released proof policy, the first 156 events match the native trace. Offer 109 is the first different event. G3 offers the totality axiom on a pair of ticket terms while native offers an instance involving saved service state. Through the second decision, the two solvers go on to make the **same multiset of 206 offers and 101 assertions** between decisions two and three. The first order difference at this point still leaves them the same work to do. At decision three, native chooses the negative literal for `le(next_ticket,next_ticket)`, which contradicts the reflexivity axiom. G3 chooses a negative equality between conditional service terms. Following decision three, native offers 58 more candidates and asserts 26 lemmas before its next decision. G3 offers none in that interval.

To measure the effect of that choice, the scratch queue selected the native atom once from g3's activity heap after verifying membership and an undefined assignment. G3 continued to choose its own phases and all later decisions. Seven rotating, GC-off runs counted instructions on the solver thread with tree logging disabled. Separate logged runs supplied event counts and every complete verification matched the reference.

| History or intervention | Decisions | Offers | Asserted lemmas | 4/55 check, M instructions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Current release | 159 | 1,913 | 531 | 53.95 |
| Choose the native reflexive atom on decision 3 | 106 | 1,553 | 441 | 45.63 |
| Choose it on decision 5 | 69 | 1,105 | 388 | 38.20 |
| Run sibling 4/17 through ordinary g3 | 118 | 2,321 | 689 | 66.80 |
| Run all siblings through ordinary g3 | 45 | 887 | 356 | 34.19 |

The decision-5 intervention uses the fourth ordinary heap extraction because a random choice bypasses that extraction. An attempted reverse substitution on the other history failed the eligibility check and contributed no measurement. The old 4/17 intervention had saved work on an earlier release; it increases current check cost by 23.75%. Even the best one-decision substitution saves only 15.75M instructions on a complete roughly 2.6B-instruction verifier.

### Which search changes transfer?

Across four rotated whole-verifier rounds, increasing the initial activity of all syntactically diagonal binary predicates saved 2.91% of Hybrid instructions and **increased ARM by 33.96%**. Restricting it to variables created during search gave ARM +34.63%. Restricting it to variables created outside search gave POPL18 −1.75% and liveness Ticket +2.99%. A separate experiment recognized a positive universal reflexivity axiom and asserted its consequences for the existing constants of that sort. It gave POPL18 **−7.02%** and nested Ticket **+7.18%**. The production solver keeps its existing decision and assertion order.

Across the whole 4/55 search the transitivity axiom alone accounted for 234 offers versus 114 native. Two uniqueness axioms for the live and saved ticket relations contributed another 154 excess offers. We tested replacing a relation known to be single-valued with a unary function plus a definedness predicate, or with a function plus the original binary predicate as a guard. The complete defining axiom must be a positive premise. A partial relation may have no value at an input, so the definedness condition matters. Nine independent Ticket snapshots ran fresh and with a push before the goal in both CLIs. Incremental L2S 12/8 fell from 277M to 226M g3 instructions with the unary definedness predicate. L2S 14/8 rose from 205M to 1,815M and POPL18 4/55 rose from 231M to 460M. All 324 checks concluded UNSAT.

### Can arithmetic replace quantified order axioms?

The scratch rank encoding recognizes positive reflexivity, totality and transitivity premises for the same binary predicate. For the tested pure first-order UF inputs, a countable satisfying model suffices. Quotienting a total preorder by mutual comparability in both directions gives a countable linear order, which embeds in the rationals. Assigning each value its class's real-valued rank represents the original relation as `rank(x) <= rank(y)`. Antisymmetry, if asserted, stays in the formula. In the reverse direction any rank interpretation induces a total preorder. This reasoning depends on the source fragment. The live diagnostic used known pure inputs and lacks a production eligibility check.

A second encoding used a unary membership predicate for the image of a linear order in the reals. It restricted quantified variables to that image and constrained function results of the represented sort. Finite enumeration checked every binary relation on domains of sizes one through four. Exactly 1, 3, 13 and 75 total preorders, respectively, admitted a rank assignment. Both CLIs passed the three-element chain, contradictory cycle and tied-rank controls for their supported encodings. On a satisfiable order with no greatest element, the 0.8-second checks timed out; they provide no empirical answer on infinite models.

| Independent g3 replay, M instructions | Original | Rank | Restricted image |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Nested 16/1, fresh | 1,292 | 373 | 473 |
| Nested 16/1, incremental push | 520 | 384 | 443 |
| POPL18 4/55, fresh | 222 | 235 | 383 |
| POPL18 4/55, incremental push | 231 | 201 | 369 |

Five pinned normal-GC pairs tested a live AST transformation in eligible single-condition batches. Complete nested Ticket saved 3.69% of instructions (436 → 423 ms) while POPL18 used **26.45% more** (397 → 504 ms). In separate GC-off batch measurements, nested 16 went from 345.89M to 249.34M instructions. POPL18 batches 6, 7 and 8 rose from 84.80M, 146.41M and 91.74M to 223.19M, 378.05M and 317.17M. The three regressions outweigh the nested win. All six complete verifier inputs matched the references. The rank and membership encodings remain experiments.

### Retained queue change and corpus ranking

Commit `24e06cb87` finishes a registered candidate immediately when the checker has already satisfied its body. At that point the prepared instance owns no temporary AST reference. The queue previously entered materialization, looked up the rewriter and released empty locals. Preparation also queried the quantifier kind separately just before reading its body through an accessor that already checks the kind. The public preparation and materialization interfaces retain their separate lifetimes and error checks.

Nine rotating pairs of 120,000 calls used the registered candidate benchmark, with matching zero allocations. At clause width four, first- and last-binding cases saved **12.21% and 7.61% of instructions**. At width sixteen they saved **12.20% and 3.02%**. The absolute difference was about 302 instructions per candidate throughout. Normal-GC complete verification showed smaller, mixed effects. POPL18 used 1.34% more instructions in the first seven-pair panel and 0.31% fewer in the nine-pair repeat on another CPU. In the latter panel nested Ticket used 0.62% fewer, Hybrid 0.27% fewer, and ARM 0.26% more. With GC off all four improved by 0.15–0.38%. All 228 verifier transcripts matched linked Z3, as did three pairs each on ordinary Raft and Apple rfn2 and dramc_nb2. The full SMT core package, the focused checked/debug/trace tests, and vet passed. [Benchmark](smtcore/smt_quantifier_candidate_benchmark_test.go)

A fresh instruction screen ran each engine once on each of the 228 historical inputs. G3 retired fewer instructions on 210. Hybrid still leads the absolute instruction deficits at 1.663B, followed by POPL18 Ticket at 1.109B, ARM at 0.927B, L2S Ticket at 0.798B, and nested Ticket at 0.713B. Elapsed rankings from this concurrently loaded screen are unsuitable for claiming workload wins. Rotated pairs above give the separate elapsed controls.

### Two arithmetic checks costing more than ten times native

Number theory and gcd2 showed 335M and 306M excess instructions per complete verifier run. They are related specifications. The original SMT-LIB for four selected obligations is byte-identical across the pair. Three full-process sample profiles per engine found 238M and 231M g3 instructions under pending assertion internalization, against approximately 48M and 44M native. Arithmetic comparison rewriting accounted for about 71M and 63M g3 instructions inclusively. These stack categories overlap.

Five GC-off runs measured the actual incremental check windows. The ordinary-g3 control used the same pre-push policy, then used the direct solver check after each push. On number theory, all check windows together cost **354.03M release / 293.30M ordinary g3 / 80.37M native**. The corresponding gcd2 figures were 337.23M / 280.05M / 77.08M. Two particularly short native checks expose both costs.

|---|---:|---:|---:|

On incremental 2/25 and 2/30 the solvers matched decisions, conflicts, quantifier instances and resource steps exactly. Each took zero decisions and one conflict, with four and ten instances respectively. The direct CLI results include process startup and do not measure the live private-proof overhead. The next investigation can now use 2/25 and 2/30 to price unproductive private attempts, and ordinary g3 to identify the extra cost of preparing and rewriting the same arithmetic terms across the other checks. ### Arithmetic witness searches on number theory and gcd2

Commit `aa0392774` lets the incremental solver handle a quantified goal when the private witness planner finds only positive universals in one eligible arithmetic domain. In that case the query supplies no counterexample witness to guide the one-round tuple search. This is a performance heuristic. An ordinary check still proves or refutes the original goal. Mixed eligible domains and quantifiers supplying a counterexample witness retain the existing search.

Across the 228 historical verifiers, 120 private witness plans actually ran. All ten single-domain arithmetic attempts missed. The two related specifications share the measured inputs, so these are five distinct attempts repeated twice. All 61 successful witness refutations used other sorts. On number theory, check 2/3 ran one full attempt. Checks 2/25 and 2/30 each ran a selected and a full attempt. Both approximations returned SAT even though the original query was UNSAT. Their combined costs were about 18.75M and 22.60M solver-thread instructions. Benchmarking the admission call on saved 2/25 and 2/30 dropped allocation from 3.01 and 3.16 MB to 632 and 728 bytes per call. The Apple and Raft witness benchmarks preserved their expected proof counts. [Captured-query benchmark](api/api_witness_instances_benchmark_test.go)

All check windows together fell from 354.03M to 299.26M on number theory and from 337.23M to 282.55M on gcd2. A broader domain filter gave similar complete results in seven pairs. We kept the narrower rule because the measurements only implicate the unopposed universals.

All 228 release transcripts matched linked Z3, including stdout, stderr and exit status. Ordinary Raft, Apple rfn2 and Apple dramc_nb2 also matched in three release pairs each. ### Recognizing integer bounds that are already in normal form

For `x <= n` or `f(x) >= n`, an uninterpreted integer term has coefficient one, and a small integer bound on the right has no variable to cancel. The old reducer tested powers, built the two monomial lists, looked for shared products and tried several further rules before returning the original expression. Commit `f9bb2d021` identifies this case before polynomial reduction. Strict inequalities still go through negation. The signed 32-bit minimum goes through ordinary cancellation because negating it can allocate a larger numeral. This optimization applies inside quantified bodies as well as to ground terms.

Five benchmark samples put a bound on an integer variable at **1,151 → 86 ns** and one on an uninterpreted constant at **1,219 → 103 ns**. Both went from two allocations to zero. The strict comparison control used zero allocations throughout. Three weaker experiments also reduced instruction counts on the target checks. Combining AST identity reads saved about 6–7M instructions over all the checks in each verifier, using stack storage for singleton monomials saved another 1M, and exiting only the cancellation routine for atomic operands saved about 4M on its own. Recognizing the normal form at comparison entry saved **26–27M**. Only the comparison-entry change was retained. [Reducer and monomial benchmarks](ast/rewriter/arith_polynomial_benchmark_test.go)

| Complete verifier, eleven rotated runs | Starting g3 | Witness change | Both changes | Linked Z3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Number theory, median instructions | 838.05M | 767.94M | **737.28M** | 512.60M |
| Number theory, median elapsed | 171.36 ms | 136.39 ms | **130.09 ms** | 101.29 ms |
| gcd2, median instructions | 814.14M | 739.03M | **711.15M** | 504.88M |
| gcd2, median elapsed | 140.91 ms | 127.52 ms | **123.97 ms** | 96.48 ms |

The combined changes saved **12.0% and 12.7% of complete instructions**. In a second seven-pair run on another CPU, the comparison shortcut alone saved 3.95% and 4.25%. Results outside arithmetic were mixed. In nine pairs the shortcut moved instructions by −0.40% on Hybrid, +0.25% on POPL18 Ticket, +0.46% on ARM and −0.06% on liveness Ticket. Hybrid took 7.3% longer in that concurrent timing panel and 0.08% longer in the repeat, which measured +0.17% instructions. These controls establish no elapsed improvement on Hybrid.

All 228 final release transcripts and three complete pairs each on Raft and the two Apple isolates matched the native reference. The rewriter, SMT core and API suites passed against the combined changes. The checked/debug/trace arithmetic tests and rewriter vet passed. The original and new CLIs produced identical simplifications for 474 comparisons in four option settings, including reversed operands, powers of two at the integer representation boundary, Real rationals, coercions, modulus and strict inequalities. Four captured queries retained identical decisions, conflicts, quantifier instances and resource counts in fresh and incremental g3 replay.

**Where time remains.** Five GC-off runs put all number-theory check windows at **272.67M versus 80.37M** native. On 2/25 the original 25.34M is now 5.25M versus 1.70M. On 2/30 the original 33.70M is now 9.78M versus 2.95M. Three whole-process profiles put inclusive comparison rewriting at roughly 34M and 28M instructions for the two specifications, down from 71M and 63M. On number theory, pending assertion internalization still accounted for about 176M, including 142M in reduction and 52M in macro discovery. Native pending assertion internalization sampled about 48M. These are overlapping stack estimates.

The largest remaining number-theory check gaps are 2/39 (24.77M versus 6.28M) and 2/22 (26.23M versus 7.91M). Across 96 fresh and incremental CLI runs on eight captures, both engines returned UNSAT throughout. On incremental number-theory 2/39 they matched seven decisions, six conflicts and one quantifier instance, but g3 charged **9,863** resource steps versus **7,169** native. On 2/22 the counts were 3/2/0 in both engines and 2,950 versus 2,617 steps. The next comparison should count assertion rewrites, macro expansion and nonlinear arithmetic theory calls in those windows. The same goal index in gcd2 can be a different obligation. Its 2/39 takes zero decisions, one conflict and 1,222 steps in both engines. ### Why Gröbner reduction exhausted arithmetic check budgets early

On number-theory 2/39, both engines report 177 arithmetic max/min operations, 32 nonlinear bound operations, 27 Horner operations and four Gröbner computations. On 2/22 the counts also match at 30, 3, 7 and 6. We counted each increment to the g3 resource limit with a Go source overlay and each native increment at the two overloads of `reslimit::inc` in this fork's release binary. Each stack census sums to the solver's published count. A check for cancellation consumes a resource step here. Z3 checks at the end of a reduction pass only when the pass changed an equation. G3 also checked after every unsuccessful pass.

| Incremental number-theory goal | Old g3 steps | Z3 steps | Inside polynomial reduction, g3 / Z3 | Other Gröbner steps, both | Outside Gröbner, both |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2/22 | 2,950 | 2,617 | 388 / 55 | 600 | 1,962 |
| 2/36 | 3,846 | 3,615 | 260 / 29 | 405 | 3,181 |
| 2/37 | 3,307 | 3,025 | 309 / 27 | 471 | 2,527 |
| 2/39 | 9,863 | 7,169 | 2,838 / 144 | 3,884 | 3,141 |

**User-visible effect.** Eight original SMT queries ran fresh and with a push, each with an unlimited budget and five limits derived from native's unlimited count. Across these 96 configurations the old g3 matched 44 native answers. The corrected g3 matched all 96 answers, resource counts, decisions, conflicts and quantifier instance counts. At a 7,169-step limit on 2/39 the release verdict changed from `unknown` to `unsat`. At 3,584 steps both still return `unknown`. The archive preserves the original scripts and each of the 288 executions. [CLI regression input](cmd/g3/test_vectors/grobner_bounded_reduction.smt2) · [Native reduction loop](../src/math/grobner/grobner.cpp)

Commit `4546cd835` also fixes an independent scope defect. On the first matching monomial of an older equation, g3 copied the equation and could leave the copy unchanged. On a complete miss the scope comparison could retry forever. The corrected implementation reduces the copied monomial, preserves the previously scanned prefix in its new owner, and returns immediately after a complete miss. The tests cover a copied prefix, a miss against an older equation and restoring the base equation after pop. Both the wrongly charged miss and the unchanged copy reproduced before the fix. [Reducer and scope regressions](math/grobner/grobner_test.go)

**Instruction costs.** An unsuccessful reduction now builds no survivor list. Two monomials of equal degree divide one another exactly when their sorted products agree. A one-variable divisor needs only an identity search for that factor. Five rotations of the unmatched-rule benchmark on one CPU, with two-monomial target equations, measured the following medians.

| Shape | Old | Fixed reduction loop | Plus factor matching |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Linear vs linear | 84 ns | 52 ns | 11 ns |
| Quadratic vs quadratic | 87 ns | 53 ns | 11 ns |
| Linear vs quadratic | 86 ns | 52 ns | 12 ns |

The original fixtures allocated 16 B once per attempt, and the retained code allocated zero. Across five GC-off live-verifier runs, 2/39 dropped from 24.76M to 24.14M instructions with the loop fix alone and to **21.38M** with factor matching. Z3 took **6.28M**. Likewise 2/22 went from 26.22M through 25.94M to **23.84M**, versus **7.91M** native. Correcting the resource count explains all the excess steps here, but only a small fraction of the excess instructions. The combined release saved 9.15M instructions across all check windows on number theory and 8.43M on gcd2.

Eleven rotated normal-GC complete runs put number theory at **734.47M → 721.78M** instructions, versus 511.61M Z3, and gcd2 at **709.50M → 699.18M**, versus 504.06M Z3. The corresponding median times were 130.1 → 128.5 vs 95.2 ms and 126.2 → 123.0 vs 94.0 ms. A second eleven-run release panel saved 1.12% and 1.35% of complete instructions respectively. The four short holdouts used 0.2–1.4% more instructions in their nine-pair panel. All 228 reference transcripts and three pairs on each of Raft, Apple rfn2 and Apple dramc_nb2 matched. The ordinary Gröbner and SMT core suites, end-to-end bounded CLI regression, checked/debug/trace Gröbner suite and Gröbner vet passed.

**What to target next.** Instruction samples from 80 incremental CLI replays per query and engine put the 2/39 nonlinear arithmetic final check at about 8.28M g3 versus 2.62M native, including 6.07M vs 1.80M in Gröbner computation. Pending assertion internalization took another 3.63M vs 0.88M. At 2/22 the Gröbner figures were 2.29M vs 0.56M, including 0.91M vs 0.16M building intervals for monomials. These inclusive samples include depth and unwinding uncertainty. They are separate from the live-verifier counters. G3 spent about 1.53M instructions in superposition on 2/39. Reading AST IDs directly from the arena and removing the separate ID cache saved 0.89M in that check, but the nine-pair complete run used 0.12% more instructions on number theory and 0.41% more on gcd2. That variant remains an experiment. Compare interval construction and temporary monomial ownership with native on the same terms. Pending assertion work is another distinct target. ### November 27 — Nonlinear interval products

Counting entries in g3 with a source observer and in this fork's native Z3 with debugger breakpoints found the same arithmetic work in both engines. On number theory 2/22 each built 177 monomial intervals and multiplied 229 factors inside those calls. On 2/39 the counts were 136 and 216. The ordinary and square inconsistency checks revisited 87 monomials on 2/22 and 60 on 2/39 within the same equation. A source observer was needed for the Go counts because some debugger breakpoints hit more than once per entry.

G3 previously made a heap object per temporary endpoint product and grew a slice of pointers to release them. Two positive intervals need two endpoint products and two mixed intervals need at most four. A local four-element array preserves arithmetic, dependency handling and cleanup order. Five alternating benchmark pairs on a pinned CPU gave these medians.

| Bounds | Before | Four local slots | Allocations before → after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| [2, 3] × [2, 3] | 269.9 ns | 146.0 ns | 72 B / 4 → 0 |
| [−2, 3] × [−2, 3] | 461.8 ns | 235.3 ns | 152 B / 7 → 0 |

In five GC-off live-verifier pairs, 2/22 fell from 23.85M to 22.94M instructions and 2/39 from 21.41M to 21.17M. All checks together fell from 263.48M to 261.76M on number theory and from 248.00M to 246.38M on gcd2. Across nine rotating complete runs with normal GC, number theory fell from 733.78M to 720.43M instructions (169.25 to 168.90 ms) and gcd2 from 702.34M to 696.01M (123.14 to 122.48 ms). All 228 corpus exit codes and output streams matched the references. A separate retention regression showed that resetting the arithmetic dependency manager left old bounds reachable through the node slice's backing array. Reset now clears the used slots. The interval timing panel predates that independent fix.

A strategy control turned off nonlinear Gröbner reasoning for four incremental CLI replays. Three pinned runs per configuration showed 2/22 still proved UNSAT and g3 saved 1.8% of whole-process instructions. On 2/36, 2/37 and 2/39 both engines changed from UNSAT to unknown. On 2/39 g3 rose from 60.10M to 22.84B instructions. Disabling nonlinear branching kept the four proofs but increased g3 instructions on all four. Keep the existing strategies. [Source observers, controls, benchmarks and raw results](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-interval-products.tar.xz)

**Direct construction of monomial products.** Native Gröbner superposition multiplies directly into the destination coefficient, appends the known factors to the destination and takes one reference per factor. The g3 prototype did the same in the internal product constructor. In five samples of the one-factor-times-one-factor benchmark, median time fell from 832 to 537 ns, allocated bytes from 248 to 184, and allocations from eight to five. On nine alternating complete verifier pairs after the interval and retention fixes, number theory used 717.58M → 715.29M instructions and gcd2 used 698.42M → 698.82M. Median times rose from 128.23 to 132.11 ms and from 126.53 to 130.61 ms. These wall times are sensitive to host load. The mixed complete-run result leaves the prototype in the experiment archive. Pending assertion internalization on 2/39 has a substantially larger measured instruction gap.
