### November 27 — Matched assertion work on nonlinear arithmetic

In the two captured incremental number-theory queries, count only calls inside pending assertion internalization. Count ordinary proof-free theory-rewriter calls inside its assertion-reduction phase. Go source observers and breakpoints on the corresponding compiled methods in this repository's Z3 give identical counts in each column.

| Check | Formulas passed to internalization | Boolean variable constructors | Enode constructors | Theory term visits | Application-frame calls |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2/22, either engine | 10 | 27 | 36 | 411 | 332 |
| 2/39, either engine | 16 | 28 | 37 | 786 | 573 |

The 80-replay instruction profiles put 2/39 assertion reduction at 2.98M g3 versus 0.65M native and subsequent formula internalization at 0.59M versus 0.22M. Reduction thus accounts for about 85% of the 2.75M pending-assertion gap. Within g3 the value-propagation pass cost approximately 1.22M, explicit reduction 0.63M, BV sharing including its reduction 0.48M and NNF 0.31M. These are sampled estimates on the earlier profiled arithmetic release. Exact call counts come from separate runs. About 1.38M of the g3 reduction instructions fell under arena AST-manager or activity-cache calls. The largest individual entry was cancellation polling at 0.10M, followed by reading a rational numeral at 0.094M and inserting a scoped substitution at 0.084M. Even eliminating an entire one of those calls could recover only a small part of this gap.

**Two rewriter prototypes.** Reading application kind and family together in three arithmetic recognizers saved 0.04–0.75% of total instructions on four isolated inputs (seven rounds, 24 incremental queries and resets per process). In nine rotating complete runs it saved 1.38% on number theory, added 0.04% on gcd2, saved 0.06% on Hybrid and added 0.98% on POPL18 Ticket. Testing parent-declaration equality before associativity and reference count in the traversal had mixed signs across the four captures and six complete inputs. All complete runs checked stdout, stderr and exit status. Neither change was retained.

**Algorithmic controls.** Three runs per engine and configuration kept all four original incremental proofs. On 2/39 adding equation elimination to an explicit simplify/SMT tactic reduced g3 instructions from 71.64M to 66.71M, still above 59.69M through ordinary incremental SMT. The other three were all more expensive through the equation-elimination tactic. Enabling polynomial sum-of-monomials normalization, sum sorting, or multiplication hoisting did little relative to explicitly setting the same option false. Moving arithmetic to the left increased 2/36 from 61.24M to 70.67M. The explicit false controls matter because just processing a global rewriter option costs several million instructions in these short-lived CLI processes.

A separate offline control replaced only positive universally quantified conjuncts with true, resolving let aliases at conjunction roots. UNSAT of this weakening proves UNSAT of the original. Both engines still proved all four goals. G3's three-run whole-process medians fell from 48.05M to 47.30M on 2/22, 55.20M to 51.33M on 2/36, 53.68M to 52.23M on 2/37 and 59.66M to 59.20M on 2/39. Explicit QF_NIA on the weakened queries was more expensive on every query in a single-run screen. The captures show some opportunity on 2/36 but little prospect of recovering the 2/39 gap merely by choosing another tactic or omitting these quantified premises. [Inputs, modes, counters, profiles and prototype sources](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-assertion-operation-costs.tar.xz)

**Which workloads still matter most?** Five rotating pairs on the same core, with ordinary GC, used fresh matching frontend builds of g3 and linked Z3 and verified both streams and exit status. Among these eight historically slow cases, Hybrid has an instruction deficit more than eight times as large as number theory. This is a targeted panel, not a fresh ranking of all 228 inputs.

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Hybrid broadcast | 1,057 | 828 | 1,727 |
| POPL18 Ticket | 383 | 239 | 1,121 |
| ARM rules3 | 451 | 331 | 981 |
| Nested Ticket | 419 | 329 | 776 |
| POPL18 alternating bit | 368 | 291 | 577 |
| Flash2 (examples/ivy) | 666 | 626 | 346 |
| Number theory | 125 | 93 | 210 |
| gcd2 | 121 | 93 | 195 |

Three additional complete runs per engine measured solver-thread instructions with GC off. Summing each phase within each run before taking medians gave 852.6M excess instructions in Hybrid checks and 581.1M in the first physical push of each batch. Later pushes together added only 0.4M. POPL18 showed 634.7M excess in checks and 164.6M on first pushes. ARM showed 610.0M and 165.7M. The early g3 proof attempts cost 331.2M, 115.2M and 144.5M respectively and can avoid subsequent checks. The normal-GC process times above cover all work, including assertion, simplification, frontend and callbacks outside those windows.

ARM has a particularly concentrated opportunity: batch 6 accounts for about 515M excess check instructions plus 117M on its first push. Checks 6/5 and 6/6 account for 116M and 111M of this and already have matched search-event studies. A separate check, 8/1, used 186.88M versus 94.93M. If search counts differ, replay the first divergent choice before changing shared hot paths. ## November 27 — ARM macro expansion and finite-model checks

On ARM batch 6, finding and expanding macros accounted for 72.0M of the 117M excess instructions on the first push. Filtering out expensive definitions made the complete proof slower. On Hybrid, value propagation exceeded even the macro gap. The paired substitution-read counts below identify repeated work in its reverse sweep.

| First-push pass | ARM batch 6 g3 / Z3, M instructions | Hybrid, all first pushes g3 / Z3, M instructions |
|---|---:|---:|
| Find macros | 107.84 / 35.80 | 298.14 / 186.34 |
| Propagate values | 27.50 / 8.16 | 196.92 / 68.98 |
| Pattern inference | 4.58 / 1.78 | 107.79 / 41.09 |
| NNF/CNF | 4.33 / 1.37 | 94.27 / 34.38 |

The hardware counts are medians of three rotated GC-off runs, summed over invocations inside each first push. The earlier external push counters include entry and setup outside the g3 pass observer. Three ARM batch-6 definitions had depth 14 and 66–71 nodes each. They expanded at 62, 54 and 36 use sites. Keeping definitions deeper than 3, 5, 8 or 12 asserted as quantified formulas increased complete ARM instructions to 6.34×, 4.56×, 2.45× and 1.84× the default, respectively. Rechecking for unchanged expansions before the final traversal and compiling substitution plans for binder-free bodies both gave mixed changes around 1% or less. Enabling quasi-macros or pulling nested quantifiers also failed to yield a transferable win.

**ARM search and replay.** During live batch 8 goal 1, g3 and linked Z3 made 886 / 947 decisions, found 50 / 54 conflicts, produced 358 / 331 quantifier instances and performed 6 / 5 final checks. Sampling only that check attributed 1,262 of 3,111 g3 samples and 769 of 1,527 native samples to model checking. These are inclusive samples across six runs. The external solver-call counters measured 187M / 95M instructions. The incremental command-line replay, with macro finding enabled and the first assertion preceding push, instead produced exactly 783 decisions, 53 conflicts, 199 instances and 52,067 resource steps in both engines. Its whole-process counters measured 253M / 109M instructions. Replay isolates the cost of matching logical work, but its profile overweights universe restrictions compared with the live check.

**Finite tables.** During live ARM 8/1 all 259 table queries returned a definite result. Scalar checks certified 210 bodies and found 19 witnesses, consuming 23.45M instructions including setup. Decision diagrams certified 27 more and found three witnesses in 2.68M. Across complete Hybrid, 4,912 scalar certificates consumed 362.45M and 641 scalar witnesses consumed 39.46M. Seven diagram certificates and two diagram witnesses cost 2.38M combined. Another 338 queries fell back during compilation after 12.63M instructions. A trial that stopped after the first failing quantifier saved 3.62% on ARM but changed Hybrid's transcript in all three runs and raised its cost from 7.45B to 11.70B instructions. Limiting failures to four increased Hybrid and nested-ticket costs by 1.5% and 3.8%.

Separate counter runs metered one internal phase per invocation. Median totals across three runs are shown below. Evaluation includes witness recovery and deferred cleanup on that path. Counter instrumentation and early-return cleanup differ between this observer and the per-result observer above.

| Finite-table phase | Complete Hybrid, M instructions | ARM 8/1, M instructions |
|---|---:|---:|
| Setup before term compilation | 12.58 | 1.00 |
| Compile terms and model functions | 169.15 | 6.98 |
| Construct binder domains | 47.73 | 3.42 |
| Evaluate tuples or diagram and recover result | 190.87 | 14.87 |

Two scratch evaluators tested whether the scalar loop could recover much of this cost. Updating only the bindings modified by the tuple counter changed complete-verifier instructions by +0.03% Hybrid, +1.47% ARM, −0.92% POPL18 and −0.24% nested Ticket. Evaluating variable and constant children directly in their parent gave +0.19%, +0.10%, −1.08% and −0.08% respectively. Seven rotated runs of each version matched all four reference transcripts. Both prototypes remain in the archive.

**What the reverse value-propagation sweep reads.** A diagnostic build recorded the result of each term lookup in the assertion substitution, separately for each assertion and direction. Across all Hybrid propagation passes, 2,973 of 3,554 reverse rows started with the same formula as their forward row, left it unchanged in both directions, and queried exactly the same set of keys. Every one of the 30,127 reverse lookups on those rows missed. These rows accounted for 86.6% of all 34,792 reverse lookups. ARM had 681 such rows out of 1,042 and 10,321 out of 16,270 lookups. The reverse sweep did change 87 Hybrid and 133 ARM rows. The measured opportunity is to avoid revisiting individual unaffected rows. The observer records only actual substitution calls. A shortcut would have to account for dependencies hidden by an internal rewrite-cache hit, substitutions from the outer scope, proof production, resource charging and cancellation. A scratch binary then skipped exactly these reverse row positions using the recorded per-input schedule. Across seven pinned pairs, complete instructions changed by −0.73% Hybrid, +0.23% ARM, −1.15% POPL18 and +0.54% nested Ticket. All reference transcripts matched. Even with eligibility supplied for free, this saved little on Hybrid. A production dependency index has low priority. The measured row counts span every propagation pass, whereas the first-push pass counters above cover a narrower interval.

**Retained auxiliary-query change.** Ordinary auxiliary checks previously built a slice of cleanup closures and allocated arrays for witness recovery before knowing whether a witness existed. Commit `bc0c7dabd` scopes temporary references to the negated assertion and delays witness allocations. Seven alternating, pinned benchmark pairs measured the following medians.

| Query | Before → after ns/op | B/op | Allocations/op |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Incremental | 8,690 → 8,317 | 1,298 → 1,106 | 25 → 15 |
| Private | 3,610 → 3,471 | 104 → 56 | 6 → 3 |

Across five complete runs, Hybrid allocated 4,003 fewer objects and 162 KB fewer bytes at the median. ARM saved 1,855 objects and 110 KB. Across nine rotations the complete-verifier instruction changes were +0.82% ARM, +0.28% Hybrid, −0.04% POPL18 and −0.15% nested ticket. The evidence supports keeping this as an allocation improvement. All 228 archived cases matched native stdout, stderr and exit status. The full 114-package Go suite passed. A separate macro-expander fault-injection regression exposed 1,032–1,448 bytes of charged, unreleased owners at nine failure positions. Commit `def6619cd` closes partially constructed traversal and substitution owners on those paths.

## November 27 — Certifying quantified bodies from uniform predicates

Commit `564907b06` reduces complete Hybrid instructions from 7.47B to 6.86B. A candidate model often interprets a predicate as true or false for every argument. For example, if the model makes `P` always false, then `P(x) ⇒ Q(x)` holds for every binding, even if `Q` varies. The SMT model checker now tries this proof before compiling function tables, constructing binder domains or searching tuples. It reads literal Boolean constant interpretations and literal defaults of functions with zero exceptional rows. It propagates true, false and unknown through the Boolean connectives. Only a proved true body discharges the query. A 96-node visit allowance bounds misses. Bounded-resource checks retain their original path. The implementation needs no persistent state or storage shared by solvers.

**Why a certificate cache had little to offer.** The observer assigned each solver and each candidate-check invocation a serial, preserving the enclosing invocation across nested checks. It compared compiled terms, functions, exceptions, defaults, sorts, integer values and ordered binder domains. Across complete Hybrid, 3,515 of 4,919 scalar and diagram certificates repeated a previously certified body in the same solver. Those repeat calls cost 286.46M instructions. Just 400 matched all compiled inputs including the concrete model values, accounting for 16.58M instructions. Comparing the compiled program and domain IDs while permitting renamed concrete values yielded 520 matches costing 24.95M. These are before any cost of validation. The observer used exact comparisons, and charged queries using a separate uninstrumented-by-comparison pass with matching phase, arity, outcome and order. Equivalent models with differently ordered tables can fall outside the counts.

**Why check the original AST.** A scratch version proved uniformity after compiling the finite tables. It recognized 4,483 Hybrid queries and saved 2.44% of complete instructions. Checking the AST directly also discharges some queries with an unsupported expression in an irrelevant branch. On the original Hybrid search path it proved the same 4,483 table-certified queries plus 309 that previously needed ordinary auxiliary solving. Across the four verifiers, all 5,080 queries certified by both paths agreed. For the 313 additional queries (309 Hybrid and four nested Ticket), the ordinary auxiliary solver returned UNSAT in every case. The fork's native Z3 executable independently returned UNSAT on all 46 distinct serialized auxiliary questions. The differential test checks that an absent predicate default yields unknown. For uniform and exceptional interpretations it verifies each definite Boolean result by instantiating the binder both ways and running the ordinary model evaluator.

| Complete verifier | Previous g3, M instructions | Current g3 | Linked Z3 | Previous / current / Z3 elapsed, ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Hybrid | 7,471 | 6,861 | 5,824 | 1,054 / 1,001 / 825 |
| ARM | 3,140 | 3,138 | 2,189 | 453 / 461 / 337 |
| POPL18 Ticket | 2,610 | 2,571 | 1,479 | 393 / 395 / 238 |
| Nested Ticket | 2,909 | 2,903 | 2,177 | 437 / 468 / 368 |

These are medians for the initial implementation (`564907b06`) across nine pinned three-engine rotations with normal GC. Another nine paired runs on a second CPU saved 7.91% of Hybrid instructions (7.462B → 6.872B) and 1.9% elapsed. The other three short controls showed little instruction change and longer median elapsed in that repeat. Across five runs Hybrid allocated 9.04 MB and 72,225 fewer objects per complete process. Seven pinned benchmark pairs on an eight-element sort and two binders dropped from 4,718 to 274 ns/op (17.2×), from 360 to zero B/op and from seven allocations to zero. All 228 reference stdout, stderr and exit statuses matched after supplying the study's ABC binary for seven model-checker cases. The SMT core and API suites, checked/debug/trace model tests and SMT vet passed.

Across three paired runs each, the ordinary Raft, rfn2 and dramc_nb2 holdouts matched their linked-Z3 reference transcripts. Raft instructions dropped from 17.68B to 16.86B (4.6%). The two Apple instruction medians stayed within 0.01% of their baselines. Median elapsed rose from 2.53 to 2.59 s on Raft, 1.48 to 1.51 s on rfn2 and 16.32 to 17.04 s on dramc_nb2 in these runs. These elapsed measurements overlap other study activity.

**Selecting the final implementation.** Eleven alternating pairs measured higher median user cycles on POPL18 (+3.92%), nested Ticket (+2.16%) and ARM (+2.08%) with the first implementation, alongside the Hybrid saving (−3.78%). Commit `4c4089c85` carries the fixed manager, model, Boolean sort and remaining visit budget together through recursive calls. It checks the result sort after finding a literal predicate value. Against the first implementation, nine paired runs on each of two CPUs reduced median user cycles on all four inputs. Against the original baseline, Hybrid saved 7.39% and 6.13% of cycles, POPL18 saved 0.36% and 0.65%, and ARM saved 0.09% and 1.63%. Nested Ticket was mixed (−0.70% and +2.39%). These are per-round ratios; whole-process elapsed time varied considerably between runs. We have not established a nested Ticket speedup. The same 228-case panel passed on this final layout. The machine-code section of the measured prototype was byte-identical to the final build from the checked-in source. The final pinned benchmark was 5,403 → 305 ns/op, a 17.7× improvement, with seven allocations eliminated.

In the final 13-rotation three-engine Hybrid comparison on CPU 23, the baseline, final g3 and linked Z3 measured **1,052 / 975 / 836 ms**, **7.472 / 6.860 / 5.821 billion instructions**, and **4.215 / 3.883 / 3.253 billion user cycles**. The change removed 37.1% of the original instruction gap. An earlier seven-rotation final build comparison overlapped other jobs and measured 1,101 / 1,172 / 853 ms despite nearly identical instruction counts. The final allocation measurement saved 9,085,096 bytes and 72,388 objects. Three paired runs of each final long holdout matched the references. Raft used 17.59B → 16.84B instructions and 2.82 → 2.42 s. The Apple changes were small in instructions: rfn2 used 11.26B → 11.24B and dramc_nb2 used 120.03B → 119.77B. Their elapsed medians were 1.77 → 1.95 s and 16.32 → 15.93 s, respectively.

**Where the gap moved.** Three GC-off solver-thread rotations reduced the Hybrid check-phase deficit from 853M to 289M instructions. Its first-push deficit was 580M. On nested Ticket, live check 16/1 now costs 261M versus 121M instructions. G3 made 1,179 decisions, installed 1,957 quantifier instances, created 3,709 Boolean variables and performed seven final checks. Linked Z3 made 671 decisions, installed 1,045 instances, created 2,057 variables and performed two final checks. POPL18 2/55 has a different signature. G3 and native both recorded zero final checks, with 872 versus 549 instantiations and a 66M instruction gap. The next search experiment should capture the first differing instantiation or decision on these two live checks and measure a controlled change across the complete verifiers. A separate opportunity remains in Hybrid preprocessing, where base assertion and first-push costs should be priced together.

## November 27 — Choosing binary counterexamples in live Ticket proofs

At baseline `a69c6fea9`, nested Ticket check 16/1 took 261M solver-thread instructions versus 121M for linked Z3. Comparing interleaved events showed that the engines agreed on the first 1,325 quantifier queue offers, 377 asserted lemmas and 261 signed Boolean decisions. The first difference appeared during validation of the candidate model. G3 produced a unary witness from finite tables while Z3 searched an auxiliary context. The trace includes auxiliary decisions. Its totals have a different scope from the outer solver statistics.

**Which witness mattered?** There were five table-generated witnesses in the first model. Five paired runs delegating just the first to ordinary restricted auxiliary search left the check at 262M instructions. Delegating the other four brought it to 110M, and all five to 103M. Three runs of each of the 32 subsets narrowed the saving to the third witness alone (78M). Changing both the first and third raised it to 269M. The second and third witnesses belonged to different binary quantifiers and shared their first ground term. For the third quantifier all six falsifying tuples shared the second term. G3 originally captured (K!64, K!63). Restricted search chose (K!63, K!63), also as a single witness. Changing that representative affected the downstream proof search.

**What transferred?** Commit `6375b910d` lets the existing restricted auxiliary solver choose a witness when at least two instances are pending and the proposed binary tuple repeats the preceding quantifier's first ground term with a different second term. The preceding quantifier must also be binary and distinct. The check runs after both model values have inverse ground representatives and before the new instance is captured. It applies on the ordinary finite-table witness-selection path. A regression test checks the fallback, its boundaries and that declining the candidate leaves the instance queue intact.

Limiting the policy to the first model increased GC-off instructions by 3.53B on Raft and 1.59B on raftok. Triggering on either shared component cost Flash 5.36% in an initial screen. Trying the second term for both binders could reproduce the nested Ticket win but missed the Raft gains. Requiring matching binder sorts cost raftok 2.75B. The retained rule saved 1.11B and 602M on the two Raft cases in a same-executable GC-off screen. All 228 paired comparisons matched the references. A separate sweep of the actual production binary matched native stdout, stderr and exit status on all 228 cases.

| Complete verifier, nine rotated runs, normal GC | Prior g3, M instructions | Final g3, M instructions | Linked Z3, M instructions | Median ms, prior / final / Z3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Nested Ticket | 2,904 | 2,688 | 2,178 | 513 / 442 / 366 |
| POPL18 Ticket | 2,588 | 2,594 | 1,477 | 410 / 404 / 249 |
| ARM | 3,125 | 3,131 | 2,201 | 486 / 485 / 350 |
| Hybrid | 6,870 | 6,862 | 5,821 | 1,002 / 1,019 / 851 |
| Flash | 5,616 | 5,612 | 6,058 | 888 / 896 / 902 |

Across three GC-off stage measurements, nested Ticket 16/1 fell to **77.93M instructions versus 121.12M for linked Z3**, a 70% reduction from baseline. Across the complete verifier the saving was 7.45% of instructions, closing 30% of the prior whole-process instruction gap. The remaining aggregate check deficit was 175M instructions. Its largest individual contributors were 12/44 (+46M) and 13/46 (+41M). Three additional paired runs per long holdout matched their references. Ordinary Raft used 16.90B → 15.81B instructions (2.63 → 2.60 s). Apple rfn2 used 11.24B → 11.21B (2.14 → 2.29 s), and dramc_nb2 used 120.02B → 119.78B (16.01 → 16.17 s). Host load varied during elapsed measurements.

**Independent POPL18 experiment.** At 2/55 the first 105 interleaved events matched. Moving one queue entry ahead of seven others reproduced the native order of a 42-entry offer batch and left the check near 95M instructions. The first five signed decisions matched. At decision six, Z3 split on a generated ticket's equality with zero, which was also unassigned and eligible in g3. Forcing this one native choice reduced the median from 95.45M to 66.72M in five runs, still above Z3's 29.01M. Making that choice at decision four produced 83.26M and at decision five 96.65M. Adding the queue reorder to the sixth-decision experiment produced 67.17M. The forced variable ID and decision index are diagnostic controls only. The next experiment should compare activity scores, insertion and removal order, and heap ties for the eligible variables leading up to decision six. Test any general explanation on the adjacent expensive goals and on the complete verifier.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| POPL18 Ticket | 2,570.2 | 2,463.4 | 1,478.4 | 379.6 | 365.2 | 238.3 |
| Nested Ticket | 2,671.6 | 2,687.6 | 2,174.5 | 386.8 | 392.9 | 328.7 |
| Liveness Ticket | 1,478.1 | 1,487.8 | 1,289.0 | 225.7 | 227.1 | 198.1 |
| test_liveness2 | 2,078.0 | 2,075.7 | 1,684.9 | 309.5 | 311.4 | 264.0 |

**Where the searches diverge.** Both engines started 2/55 with the same 101 heap members. Forty-two activity scores already differed. Three earlier obligations that g3 discharged privately cost Z3 17 search-time variable creations and random draws (6, 6 and 5). On 2/8 the first six decisions agreed. The seventh draw was 239 in native and 27,856 in g3 against a threshold of 327. The resulting paths encountered different conflicts. On 2/14 a native conflict raised variable 130's activity to 2.49048. On the sixth decision of 2/55 this equality was the native heap maximum. Its g3 score was zero. Transplanting that single score reduced the measured g3 check from 95.35M to 66.70M instructions. Transplanting a second score brought it back up to 88.41M. Removing random splits, resetting the stream per search, and two dedicated-stream variants each improved complete POPL18 slightly. They raised raftok instructions by 19–154%, ARM by 26–38% and ordinary Raft by 17–59%.

**Where equal search work still costs more.** Of 284 numbered check windows, 87 matched all nine counters and together cost g3 an extra 175M instructions. Eight more windows with counts within 10% added 31.7M. On 7/1 both solvers made 319 decisions, encountered 25 conflicts, instantiated 820 quantifiers and created 1,391 Boolean variables. G3 used 85.55M instructions against 36.75M. Sixteen check-gated profiles attributed 22.1% of g3 instruction samples to rewriting and 20.3% to assertion internalization, inclusively. The corresponding native samples were 20.3% and 14.2%. Matching the search decisions alone leaves substantial implementation cost on this workload.

**Finding a smaller proof.** Thirteen saved original obligations cover goals 37, 55 and 56 in batches 2–5, plus 7/1. Retaining the quantifier-free premises and instantiating positive universal premises at well-sorted tuples of constants from the goal proved eight with both engines. Ground premises alone proved zero. One extra constant per sort yielded no additional proofs. Dropping data congruence while retaining Boolean equality still proved three of the four goal-37 instances. Independently rechecked minimized ground cores needed only 6–29 clauses. An ordinal-based experiment that skipped the eight successful obligations priced a ceiling of 14.85% on its instrumented verifier. Running the ground proof on all twelve obligations from batches 2–5 instead raised instructions from 2.157B to 2.194B. Selecting the four guarded agreements took 2.064B in that experiment.

**What shipped.** After earlier proof attempts on eligible incremental batches are inconclusive, the solver recognizes a negated guarded equality between two uninterpreted predicates applied to the same tuple of one to four constants. It uses the existing ground projector and accepts only a proved contradiction. An inconclusive attempt falls through to ordinary solving. The private scratch belongs to this call. The code uses no spec names, ordinals or shared worker state. The bounded Boolean split refinement in `c04f9f41f` keeps the private SAT fallback. Compared with the initial `ec69f670a` version, complete POPL18 retired essentially the same instructions (2,463.1M initially), with median cycles falling from 1,416.3M to 1,391.6M. On the retained single fresh problem, five 35-iteration runs took 1.468 ms and 986.6 KB per ground check versus 0.986 ms and 166.5 KB for ordinary checking. The benefit measured here belongs to the complete incremental history. [Implementation](api/api_predicate_agreement.go) · [Regression and benchmark](api/api_predicate_agreement_test.go) · [Original SMT-LIB fixture](perf/ivy_apple/test_vectors/ticket_guarded_predicate_agreement.smt2.gz)

**Controls.** All 228 final verifier transcripts matched the reference exit status, stdout and stderr. Seven model-checking cases were rerun with the ABC executable available. Three alternating pairs per long holdout also matched. Median instructions in billions were 15.85 → 15.87 on ordinary Raft, 11.27 → 11.19 on Apple rfn2 and 119.98 → 119.99 on dramc_nb2. The complete Go suite passed on the initial implementation. The final Boolean split refinement passed the API suite, focused checked/debug/trace tests and API vet.

**Where to look next.** A diagnostic that widened ground tuple coverage and compared applications differing in at most one syntactic argument proved 2/55 in 23.1M instructions versus 29.0M native. It needed an experimental goal selector. Try using a ground candidate assignment to identify an actual violated congruence pair before generating its constraint. Measure how often those extra constraints close a proof and what failed attempts cost. Two more ground projections can use already established sibling facts. For 4/56, one instance of 4/12 sufficed. For 5/56, either 5/38 or 5/39 sufficed. G3 and native independently confirmed the consequences and the resulting contradictions. Asserting the selected facts in the ordinary live verifier raised process instructions from 2.048B to 2.065B. Retaining all preceding proofs raised it to 3.258B. Broad retention is expensive even when individual final checks get cheaper. [Drivers, measurements, profiles and projected problems](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-ticket-activity-and-ground-agreement.tar.xz)

With the final release, three instrumented rotations put 2/55 at 57.06M instructions, down from 95.48M on the previous release. Linked Z3 took 29.01M. The shortcut fires on earlier obligations and changes the later search. On 7/1 g3 still used 85.19M against 36.74M. Across all POPL18 check windows the measured excess fell from 634M to 514M instructions. First pushes still cost an extra 165M.

## November 27 — Sharing ground witnesses across guarded case proofs

Commit `4ec97665f` grounds universal premises using the constants in a guarded disjunction together with constants appearing in asserted binary relations. This exposed proofs that grounding at the goal alone had missed. Reusing the resulting SAT clauses under the same premises made the second sibling substantially cheaper. In eleven alternating, pinned, normal-GC rotations all four complete verifier inputs improved. Times include the frontend. Each engine used the same frontend and matched its reference output.

| Complete verifier | Previous g3 ms | New g3 ms | Linked Z3 ms | Previous g3 M instructions | New g3 M instructions | Linked Z3 M instructions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| POPL18 Ticket | 385.2 | 361.5 | 254.7 | 2,455.7 | 2,300.9 | 1,476.6 |
| Nested Ticket | 408.0 | 374.6 | 347.6 | 2,686.8 | 2,420.1 | 2,176.5 |
| Liveness Ticket | 241.2 | 214.1 | 209.0 | 1,497.0 | 1,293.5 | 1,287.6 |
| test_liveness2 | 329.5 | 279.9 | 276.5 | 2,081.5 | 1,751.5 | 1,681.6 |

New g3 saved 7.3%, 10.2%, 13.8% and 17.5% of median cycles respectively. Liveness Ticket and test_liveness2 are within 2.5% of native elapsed time in this run. Nested Ticket's check calls now use 754M against native's 872M. It still spends 360M versus 176M on first pushes and another 155M on early private proof attempts. On POPL18, the check-call instruction gap fell from 514M to 327M. Three GC-off rotations put siblings 2/56, 3/56 and 4/56 at 2.55M, 3.47M and 4.34M instructions respectively, against 30.50M, 12.74M and 13.34M native. Selecting more witnesses upfront costs time on some first siblings. For example, 5/55 rose from 38.99M to 46.32M.

**Which constraints pay for themselves?** On the thirteen saved ground projections both engines independently agreed on all eight UNSAT and five SAT answers. A model-guided experiment on 2/55 needed two retries and 160 of 864 possible congruence constraints. In the live Go bit encoding, model-guided selection needed three retries and 32.8M instructions. Generating constraints between applications that differ in at most one syntactic argument took 23.8M. On 2/56 the ordinary decision-depth bound prevented a third model-guided retry from finding a proof. Raising the bound recovered that proof, but complete POPL18 measured stages were still 1,632M versus 1,539M for the previous release. Preparing a fresh sparse projection on each eligible check also cost 1,539M. Reusing its instances across siblings lowered this to 1,464M.

**Which witnesses were missing?** Four goal-only projections have models even though their source obligations are UNSAT. Adding one premise constant sufficed on 3/55, 4/56 and 5/56. Two sufficed on 4/55. G3 and Z3 independently proved each reduced input. The asserted transition facts relate these constants to each other. Reading both positive and negative binary relations on a common uninterpreted sort reduced complete instrumented stages to 1,352M. Positive relations alone took 1,384M and negative relations alone took 1,425M. The rule uses the submitted formula's declarations, signs and argument sorts. It admits a bounded disjunction of conjunctive alternatives containing an equality and accepts only a contradiction of the resulting ground consequences. Each batch owns its projection and releases it at close. New premises invalidate the old projection. [Ground proof and shape checks](api/api_predicate_agreement.go) · [Witness selection](api/internal/order/ground_relation_witnesses.go)

**Standalone replay.** The retained benchmark submits the two original 2/55 and 2/56 obligations on a fresh solver each iteration. Across five samples of twelve iterations, the ordinary incremental solver took 78.14 ms per pair, a fresh projection per goal took 27.13 ms, and the shared projection took 21.13 ms. Shared projection allocated 8.42 MB and about 60,973 objects per pair versus 13.06 MB and 95,850 objects with fresh projections. Regression tests cover positive and negative relation premises, a SAT sibling between two proved siblings, a changed premise, binary disjunction trees and an ineligible disjunct. [Benchmark and regressions](api/api_predicate_agreement_test.go) · [Original pair](perf/ivy_apple/test_vectors/ticket_guarded_case_siblings.smt2.gz)

**Controls.** All 228 production transcripts matched exit status and both output streams. Three paired rotations each of ordinary Raft, Apple rfn2 and Apple dramc_nb2 also matched. Median whole-process instructions in billions were 15.781 → 15.818, 11.225 → 11.217 and 119.920 → 119.819, respectively. In a five-round follow-up on apparent increases from the corpus screen, raftok, ip_spec1 and alternating_bit_protocol each changed by under 0.4%. ARM rules used 3,166.5M against 3,100.3M (+2.1%) across the separate builds. An instrumented repeat of all 228 cases recorded 38 successful and four inconclusive new attempts on the four workloads in the table. The instrumented ARM run recorded zero new proof attempts, and switching the rule on in the same binary gave 3,109M against 3,120M. The separate-build increase is unresolved. The API and internal order suites, focused checked/debug/trace tests and vet passed.

**The remaining 7/1 gap.** On POPL18 7/1, g3 used 85.54M check instructions against native's 36.74M. The goal is true, so the contradiction must come from the premises. Even 4,248 instances at *all* original constants admitted a model of the selected ground subset. A 51-conjunct quantified core checked by both engines includes an existential premise and a universal implication with an existential conclusion. Normalizing the original problem and creating fresh existential witnesses exposed a ground proof. Nine seed terms from facts and fresh constants still admitted a model. Expanding once to include witness-function applications produced 21 terms and a contradiction. Of twelve individual witness-function applications tried alongside the nine seeds, two independently sufficed. They apply the same existential witness function to opposite sides of a submitted equality. Greedy deletion left six terms, including one witness-function application. Both solvers proved the resulting 184 KB problem and a 61-conjunct, 19 KB core. In separate CLI measurements including parsing and reset, the six-term problem took 256M g3 instructions against 417M for the quantified original. The next experiment is to derive those witness applications in the verifier from the matching relation facts, then price their construction and failed attempts on other batches. [Experiments, proof inputs and measurements](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-ticket-case-witnesses.tar.xz)

### November 27 — Choosing existential witnesses and measuring the first push

On POPL18 Ticket batch 7, goal 1, a signed relation match finds the existential witness substitution identified by the earlier ground-core experiment. The rule examines positive and negative ground relation facts submitted by the caller. It matches the predicate, sign and position of a universally bound variable in the guard. The negative fact supplies `|__fml:k2|` and the positive fact supplies `next_ticket`. Each substitution produces an ordinary instance of the original universal implication. Its guard stays in the formula, so unmatched guard arguments cannot introduce an unsound assumption.

| Extra instances in the verifier | Median check instructions, millions |
|---|---:|
| Original g3 | 85.57 |
| Negative match alone | 97.31 |
| Positive match alone | 110.15 |
| Both matches | 62.75 |
| Both with fresh witnesses | 62.63 |
| Linked Z3, original query (previous measurement) | 36.74 |

The g3 medians cover five rotated runs pinned to one CPU, with GC disabled and hint construction inside the measured check. The combination saves 26.7% on the individual check. Knowing a substitution occurs in a sufficient ground proof tells us little about the search cost of asserting it by itself.

Scope history changes the sign of the result. On standalone replay with a push, adding both existential instances cut quantifier instantiations from 864 to 623, decisions from 217 to 115 and conflicts from 21 to 18 in **both** engines. Whole-process g3 instructions fell from 198.8M to 178.0M. Without the push, instantiations rose from 809 to 1,127, decisions from 594 to 774 and conflicts from 19 to 27. g3 rose from 442.2M to 572.9M. Identical search counters across the two engines also give a controlled example of higher g3 execution cost per unit of search. These process measurements include parsing and startup.

**Release decision.** We tested three general hint policies on twelve complete verifier workloads with normal GC and five interleaved rotations. Permitting either sign reduced median POPL18 instructions by 0.8% and increased nested Ticket by 1.1%. Requiring both signs changed the two totals by less than 0.2%. Two other experiments also produced mixed results. Merging equal ground constants before generating tuples raised POPL18 from 2.28B to 2.37B instructions in both representative orders (seven rotations). Deferring the initial conjunction rewrite reduced nested Ticket from 2.43B to 2.39B, but increased Hybrid from 6.87B to 7.02B (three rotations). Every measured verifier transcript matched the reference, including expected verification failures. All three changes remain experimental.

**First physical push.** For each verifier invocation we measured the first real Push per solver batch, summed the corresponding instruction counts, then took the median of three runs with GC disabled. The following columns measure disjoint parts of g3's push. Smaller operations such as kernel configuration are omitted.

| Workload | Initial assertion rewrite | Internalize pending assertions, including preprocessing | Quantifier propagation | Theory assignment propagation |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| POPL18 Ticket | 25.3M | 222.5M | 47.9M | 8.0M |
| Nested Ticket | 28.4M | 267.5M | 47.7M | 10.1M |
| Hybrid | 79.6M | 947.8M | 60.3M | 18.7M |
| Ticket | 18.3M | 173.6M | 29.2M | 6.8M |
| test_liveness2 | 20.9M | 191.5M | 31.0M | 7.7M |

The Boolean propagation loop accounts for just 0.11M on each of the first two workloads. In a separate matched pass measurement, POPL18 value propagation cost g3 65.77M versus Z3 21.68M, pattern inference 26.62M versus 10.57M, and NNF conversion 19.67M versus 6.64M. Nested Ticket showed a similar distribution. The 47.9M above is g3's absolute quantifier cost. Establishing how much is avoidable requires the corresponding native interval. The archived pass meters have different boundaries for their TOTAL rows, so the comparable native measurements here use individual named passes. [Drivers, three complete SMT inputs, source overlays and raw measurements](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-witness-and-push.tar.xz)

Two further observers subdivided first-push quantifier propagation. On POPL18, E-matching used 4.22M instructions, new-enode notification rounded to zero, and queue processing used 43.64M. On nested Ticket the corresponding counts were 4.83M, below 0.01M and 42.77M. Inside POPL18 queue processing, checking whether the current assignment already satisfies a candidate used 6.26M, substitution through entry to materialization used 13.84M, rewriting and finishing the lemma took 11.38M, and asserting the lemma took 10.97M. Nested Ticket repeated that distribution within 0.8M per operation. A faster pattern matcher alone could recover at most 4–5M of this work on either workload. Measure how many of these instances Z3 generates at the base scope, how many become trivial, and how often each engine reuses a substitution before optimizing any one of the three comparable downstream costs. ### November 27 — Matching first-push queue events and pricing substitution reuse

Across 84 solver batches shared by g3 and linked Z3, both engines queued **4,338 candidates**, found **2,074 already satisfied**, and asserted the other **2,264**. Neither engine deferred a candidate, served a substitution-cache hit, or rewrote an instance to true during these pushes. Within each batch, the complete sequence of event types and Boolean outcomes agreed, including enqueue order relative to the other event types. The observer does not compare the AST of each individual instance. g3 avoided four additional pushes that native performed across the six workloads. A push processes the base before the current goal is asserted, so batches can agree even when g3 proves more sibling goals before its first physical push.

| Workload | Shared pushes | Candidates | Already satisfied | Substituted and asserted | g3 substitution, M instructions | Z3 substitution, M instructions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Hybrid reliable broadcast | 34 | 1,247 | 542 | 705 | 15.13 | 5.68 |
| POPL18 Ticket | 9 | 833 | 387 | 446 | 13.74 | 5.48 |
| Nested Ticket | 13 | 982 | 491 | 491 | 13.76 | 5.51 |
| Liveness Ticket | 11 | 626 | 335 | 291 | 8.19 | 3.25 |
| test_liveness2 | 11 | 630 | 315 | 315 | 8.50 | 3.39 |
| ARM rules | 6 | 20 | 4 | 16 | 0.52 | 0.21 |

These are medians of three complete verifier runs on a pinned CPU with GC disabled. Per-instance counters bracket the corresponding operation in each implementation. The table sums those intervals within each run before taking the median. A separate build counted queue arrivals and deferrals. On POPL18, the satisfaction test cost 6.25M versus 2.08M, rewriting cost 9.03M versus 2.77M, and asserting lemmas cost 11.03M versus 3.50M. Together these four operations account for **26.22M excess instructions** on the same set of nine pushes. The cost is spread across construction, rewriting, testing and assertion. [g3 instance builder](smtcore/smt_qi_instance.go) · [Native queue](../src/smt/qi_queue.cpp)

**How much could a cheaper tuple cache recover?** A first-push-only prototype omitted the entire tuple lookup, insertion and cache-owned references. This is an experiment because dropping references changes AST lifetimes. Over five rotated runs it cut substitution from 13.75M to 13.13M on POPL18 and from 13.78M to 13.09M on nested Ticket. Those savings cover only 7–8% of the measured substitution gap. Summed first-push costs in that instrumented build changed by less than 0.1% on both. A semantics-preserving prototype which batched the tuple's reference increments also failed to save instructions there.

**Can different tuples reuse individual subterms?** A solver-local prototype remembered the results already produced by each instruction in an existing compiled ground-body traversal. It could reuse a still-live application when all its operands matched their previous values. On POPL18 this avoided 2,447 of 13,724 application constructions reached in compiled traversals. On Hybrid it avoided only 193 of 17,376. Over five rotated normal-GC runs on eight complete workloads, POPL18 used 2.307B instructions with reuse disabled and 2.309B with all arities enabled. Nested Ticket went from 2.415B to 2.433B and ARM from 3.119B to 3.155B. Restricting reuse to unary applications gave mixed results. All 120 process transcripts matched. Keep both prototypes as benchmark controls.

**Larger opportunities in the six additional holdouts.** Three rotated pairs put g3's concrete-check intervals (including any private proof attempted inside Check) at 1.345B versus 594M instructions across automatic liveness-to-safety Ticket. On 12/8 g3 used 175M versus 87M instructions despite generating fewer quantifier instances (1,983 versus 2,490) and making fewer decisions (821 versus 833). On split_queue_2_new, 11/14 alone used 76M versus 5M, although g3 asserted only 112 quantifier instances versus 99. The six archived SMT queries preserve the assertions for those holdouts. The live solver statistics and intervals come from the full incremental history. [Drivers, queries, per-instance counters and held-out verifier runs](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-first-push-queue-comparison.tar.xz)

### November 27 — When a successful private proof is slower than incremental search

On split_queue_2_new, the witness prover spent 457M instructions across its 43 calls. The ten wide witness attempts selected one sort and one round. Eight proved their obligation. On batch 11 goal 14 the attempt failed after 62.4M of the 76.4M check instructions. On the earlier sibling 11/6 it succeeded after 59.4M. Linked Z3 discharged the latter in 4.27M check instructions on its incremental solver. On automatic Ticket 12/8, by comparison, the entire g3 private attempt took 1.36M of 175.2M. These two gaps require different fixes.

**Which work to keep.** Skipping all wide single-round witness attempts saved 35% on split_queue_2_new but increased complete Hermes instructions from 23.05B to 24.93B. Limiting the candidate width to one reduced split-queue cost to about 1.11B. The more discriminating signal was how much of the base the private solver would have to translate. The ten split-queue attempts omitted 10–23% of the flattened base, compared with 29–74% on the 48 Hermes attempts. Counting only quantified premises and requiring the subset to remove half of them also rejected five Hermes attempts and raised whole Hermes cost by 1.5%.

The release uses the incremental solver when a multi-goal batch's wide, one-round, single-sort witness search would copy **more than three quarters of all base conjuncts**. The fraction is an empirical admission heuristic chosen from those two distributions. A fully grounded private UNSAT proof and the caller's ordinary incremental Check remain the decision procedures. The standalone proof path can still establish 11/6. In a 35-goal batch the regression exercises the fallback and verifies that the original solver returns UNSAT. It fails on the previous implementation because that batch starts the wide proof. [Admission](api/api_goal_instances_check.go) · [Regression](api/api_witness_premises_test.go) · [Retained benchmark](api/api_witness_instances_benchmark_test.go)

| Complete verifier, seven rotated runs | Previous g3 | Released g3 | Linked Z3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| split_queue_2_new, instructions | 1.321B | 0.862B | 0.962B |
| split_queue_2_new, elapsed | 201.53 ms | 143.99 ms | 151.45 ms |
| Hermes, instructions | 23.044B | 23.090B | 49.177B |
| Hermes, elapsed | 3.152 s | 3.124 s | 6.437 s |

All 228 complete release transcripts matched reference status, stdout and stderr. In the 11/6 microbenchmark, eight iterations per sample and five samples on one Go processor put the median standalone proof at 8.07 ms, 3.19 MB and 9,526 allocations. Deciding to fall back in the sibling batch took 24.6 µs, 14.3 KB and 46 allocations. The latter interval excludes concrete search. The complete verifier figures include it. The API suite, focused diagnostic-build tests and API vet passed. [Original input](perf/ivy_apple/test_vectors/split-queue-11-6.smt2.gz) · [Trials, raw measurements and controls](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-first-push-queue-comparison.tar.xz)

**Next target on automatic Ticket.** During 12/8, g3 spent 34.36M instructions rewriting and 39.83M asserting 1,983 instances. Z3 used 14.47M and 12.85M for 2,490. Of g3's 1,983 substitutions, 1,526 hit the tuple cache, in sharp contrast to the zero hits on first push. Those hits cost only 0.94M for substitution itself but a further **26.91M to rewrite and 31.22M to assert**. The corresponding Z3 costs after hits were 11.55M and 10.17M. The practical question is which repeated lemmas survive backtracking and what the solver must reinstall for the others. Record live clauses, bound literals, rewrite resource steps and relevant scopes before attempting reuse. Earlier experiments found that even identity rewrites can charge different resource counts on successive visits. [Earlier resource comparison](#can-repeated-quantifier-rewrites-reuse-their-old-resource-charge)

An independent eleven-rotation repeat on a second core confirmed split_queue_2_new at **200.94 ms previous g3, 144.69 ms released g3, and 150.72 ms native**. Median instructions were 1.314B, 0.868B and 0.958B respectively. The single-sort wide one-round plan appeared on only two inputs in the 228-verifier inventory. The quarter threshold separated those inputs in this corpus. Future workloads can fall on either side of that threshold, so retain both positive and negative controls.

Ordinary Raft, rfn2 and dramc_nb2 each matched the reference transcript across three previous/release rotations. Their median instruction counts changed by less than 0.4%. On dramc_nb2 the first elapsed comparison was 15.89 s previous versus 17.27 s released. Five additional alternating pairs on two other cores measured 15.47 s versus 15.67 s, 63.16B versus 63.41B cycles, and 119.97B versus 119.93B instructions.
