## November 27 — Which model binding accounts for the TLB search difference?

**Identify the terms before queue insertion.** The model-based instantiator chose eight tuples at the first differing round of TLB 60/1. Fingerprinting subsequently replaces arguments with their equality-class representatives. In the ordinary history the actual second binding of the binary tuple was a fresh processor constant, printed later as `tlb.sk0`. In the earlier unary-witness history it was the named processor `l2s_s_28`, printed later as a conditional. The model assigned the fresh and named constants the same value, `tlb.processor!val!0`, at generation zero in both inverse sets. The two unary tuples used those same alternatives. The fourth changed tuple used either a map application or a named map constant with the same model value.

**Swap one binding at a time.** Each arm ran the complete verifier. The diagnostic found the counterpart term among live enodes, checked its sort and changed the selected tuple before the checker pinned it. The control paid for the same term lookup. The table gives three-rotation median check instructions in millions, and the number of nontrivial quantified lemmas sent to the internalizer. Forward starts with ordinary search. Reverse starts with the earlier unary-witness policy.

| Binding changed | Forward, M instructions | Forward lemmas | Reverse, M instructions | Reverse lemmas |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| None | 1,096.19 | 19,943 | 906.40 | 15,038 |
| Second processor of the binary tuple | 902.14 | 14,437 | 931.40 | 15,192 |
| Processor of the first unary tuple | 1,043.86 | 17,663 | 995.64 | 17,240 |
| Processor of the second unary tuple | 1,045.34 | 17,422 | 970.03 | 16,192 |
| Map term | 1,010.59 | 16,896 | 918.85 | 14,992 |
| All four | 912.53 | 15,474 | 1,083.11 | 20,053 |

The binary tuple alone recovered 194M instructions in the ordinary history. Reversing all four swaps recovered most of the slow search. Every arm still emitted 1,086 lemmas immediately after decision 595. The substitutions affected the subsequent search even when that first expansion had the same size.

**A solver-local rule.** When a binary finite-model counterexample binds two distinct fresh uninterpreted constants of the same sort, g3 looks for a named constant for the second position. It searches the second binder's existing instantiation set in table order and requires the same generation and the same value in the completed model-evaluation cache. No new evaluation is needed. The candidate model still falsifies the quantified body on the same pair of values. The ordinary counterexample path retains and asserts the chosen ground instance.

| First fresh counter in batch 60 | Ordinary, M instructions | Named second binding, M |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 407 | 1,092.58 | 898.52 |
| 408 | 796.88 | 796.76 |
| 409 | 1,007.08 | 840.00 |
| 410 | 796.88 | 796.83 |
| 411 | 1,007.18 | 840.15 |
| 412 | 796.80 | 796.83 |
| 413 | 1,092.52 | 1,092.67 |
| 414 | 796.85 | 796.79 |

Each cell is a two-run median on the whole input with the intervention restricted to 60/1. The rule changed exactly one binding on each of three histories. Five histories retained the ordinary choice, including the expensive 413 control. Requiring a variable-equality disjunct or ranking named terms by enode parent count or class size gave no further saving on this panel.

**How often does it apply?** Across all 228 complete release inputs, 45 reached the second-binder check, four searched a set and one changed a binding. That input was TLB. All 228 exit codes and both output streams matched the reference with the rule enabled. Same-binary, ordinary-GC comparisons also matched ordinary Raft and both Apple holdouts. The three-pair median within-pair change on complete TLB was −0.44% of instructions; seven further pairs gave −0.22%. ARM moved +1.45% in three pairs and +0.08% in seven further pairs. It entered the helper three times and never searched an instantiation set. Nested Ticket moved +0.74% and +0.80% respectively, searched twice and changed zero bindings. Its observed whole-process increase remains unexplained. Raft moved +0.50% then −0.38%. Apple rfn2 moved +0.22% and dramc_nb2 −0.15% over three pairs each. These measurements support a targeted search improvement on TLB.

**Why linked Z3 is still faster on this check.** Two independent native profile runs each counted 12,605 nontrivial quantified lemmas inside 60/1. The C++ counter increments after the satisfaction check, substitution and rewrite-to-true test. Separate per-operation hardware meters in both engines confirmed the same number of internalizations. The table gives medians from three complete rotations. Each cell is the sum of calls bracketed within the selected solver-thread check, with user-mode instruction counting and GC disabled.

| Quantifier operation | Previous g3, M instructions | Released g3, M | Linked Z3, M | Released g3 calls | Z3 calls |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test whether the current assignment satisfies the instance | 85.42 | 68.98 | 39.97 | 21,113 | 18,255 |
| Substitute the ground bindings | 121.25 | 117.15 | 43.96 | 14,437 | 12,605 |
| Rewrite the substituted instance | 178.95 | 137.57 | 38.74 | 14,437 | 12,605 |
| Internalize the quantified lemma | 277.94 | 214.29 | 49.93 | 14,437 | 12,605 |

The released solver emits **14.5% more lemmas**, but each installation averages **14,843 instructions versus 3,961**. Matching the native average at g3's existing call count would recover **157.1M instructions** from installation alone. Rewrite averages 9,529 versus 3,073 instructions per call. Combined, the four measured phases explain about **365M** of the approximately **511M** remaining check gap. Substitution changed relatively little when search improved because nearly all the eliminated substitutions had already been cheap tuple-cache hits. The production run still needed 5,473 cache misses versus 5,077 in native. Different terms and clause widths can affect these averages.

The archived drivers, binding-swap logs, corpus transcript checks, release comparisons and per-operation hardware counts reproduce these measurements. The separate three-engine elapsed-time trial and call-stack sampling trial produced no usable observations. The installation totals above identify the next operation to investigate. [Benchmark sources and raw results](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-tlb-model-bindings.tar.xz)

## November 27 — What does installing a quantified lemma cost on TLB 60/1?

Every lemma reaching this path on the selected check is a disjunction. At the start of **12,197 of 14,437** installations in g3, every operand already had a Boolean binding. Linked Z3 had **10,668 of 12,605** such installations. This group cost 117.32M instructions in g3 and 27.78M in Z3. The remaining 2,240 and 1,937 installations cost 97.11M and 22.15M respectively. These are medians from two reverse-order pairs of complete verifier runs on the parent revision bf4a3f032. The signed-literal test strips one outer NOT. Scope, width and binding observations occur outside the measured operations.

| Operation, millions of solver-thread instructions | All bound, g3 | All bound, Z3 | At least one missing, g3 | At least one missing, Z3 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Internalize operands and collect their literals | 13.05 | 7.07 | 71.01 | 16.77 |
| Simplify and insert the root clause | 27.45 | 8.37 | 5.15 | 1.46 |
| Install OR relevance watches | 30.40 | 7.94 | 6.41 | 1.81 |
| Mark the root and propagate relevance | 40.30 | 5.80 | 13.16 | 2.36 |

Both engines usually simplify the all-bound disjunction to a binary clause. Of 12,197 such installations, g3 stored 11,780 ordinary auxiliary clauses of length two. Native stored 10,338 out of 10,668. Another 300 and 242 respectively added no ordinary auxiliary clause record. Watch-only and unit effects are outside that directory observation.

Search order differs, so a second comparison matched cells by original disjunction width, number of missing bindings and exact solver scope level within the check. It then applied native's mean cost in each cell to the g3 call count in that cell. The shared cells cover 7,873 all-bound and 1,373 partly unbound g3 installations. On the all-bound subset, marking and propagating relevance accounts for 21.16M excess instructions, installing watches 13.73M, inserting the clause 11.70M and collecting literals 3.28M. On the partly unbound subset, operand processing alone accounts for 31.59M. Different terms and assignments can appear at the same solver scope level. Both engines matched the reference transcript and exit code in each run.

**Reuse the existing OR watch on its first visit.** g3 already resolves each child's sign and expression-table slot while setting up the watch. It previously walked the parent AST again to recover those same operands as soon as the relevance queue reached the parent. The queue now passes the freshly built record to that particular visit. It still scans in source order, reads current assignments and invokes the same handlers. Two focused tests exercise an initial negative witness with an explicit operand assignment and a previously queued parent whose mark is cleared. The latter test exposed a difference between delivering a watch and draining the queue during prototyping.

A separate prototype reused the child's signed literal just for registering the watch. In five normal-GC pairs it changed complete TLB instructions by +0.07% and nested Ticket by +0.70%, despite savings on four other inputs. That prototype remains in the benchmark archive.

Commit `9c5709919` reduces total installation from **214.47M to 189.73M instructions (−11.54%)** across the same 14,437 lemmas in two reverse-order pairs. That leaves about 139.8M above native. The six complete inputs below each ran for five alternating normal-GC pairs. Whole-process changes are smaller. The complete corpus of 228 inputs and both Apple isolates matched their reference exit codes and both streams.

| Complete input | Change in instructions vs parent | g3 elapsed, ms | Linked Z3 elapsed, ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TLB | −0.13% | 6,063 | 8,862 |
| Raft without the additional assumption | −0.97% | 2,144 | 3,403 |
| POPL18 Ticket | −0.76% | 342 | 242 |
| ARM | +0.82% | 462 | 345 |
| Nested Ticket | −0.14% | 351 | 331 |
| Automatic Ticket | −0.24% | 430 | 312 |

Instruction changes are medians of within-pair changes. Elapsed columns are per-engine medians from a separate five-round comparison on the same inputs and frontend. In the direct parent comparison, elapsed medians ranged from +0.12% on nested Ticket to +6.38% on Raft. These trials establish a reduction in work on the targeted path. They do not establish an end-to-end elapsed improvement over the parent.

**Which fresh operands cost the most?** Timing each previously unbound operand from internalization through literal lookup identified three groups. Positive equalities cost about 33.7M instructions in g3 versus 8.38M in linked Z3 (1,260 versus 1,101 operands). Negated disjunctions cost 19.2M versus 3.99M (731 versus 518), and negated conditionals 10.1M versus 2.18M (258 versus 199). Together they account for about 48.4M excess instructions. The initial spelling of the operand matters here. A negated equality cost far less on average than a positive equality. These totals include recursive work on its children.

**Time the whole target check.** Six further rotations enabled normal GC and removed all per-lemma measurement hooks. The meter bracketed only check 60/1 in the running verifier. Median instructions and elapsed were **969.86M / 137.95 ms** on the parent, **950.77M / 132.78 ms** after the change, and **387.68M / 58.24 ms** on linked Z3. The median within-rotation change from the parent was −2.22% of instructions and −3.03% elapsed. The complete TLB input favors g3, while this individual check still takes **2.28×** the native elapsed time.

A second gate prototype resolved compound AND/OR literals from their existing child array during gate construction. In five complete pairs it changed instructions by +0.15% on TLB, +0.32% on POPL18 Ticket, +0.39% on automatic Ticket, −0.04% on nested Ticket, −0.52% on ARM and −0.51% on Raft. It remains an experiment. The archive includes both exploratory prototypes, the release benchmark, raw operation counts, matched-scope data, complete transcript checks and all six whole-check rotations. [Benchmark sources and measurements](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-quantified-lemma-installation.tar.xz)

### November 27 — Nested Boolean operands of fresh equalities on TLB 60/1

Internalizing fresh conditional children of positive equalities consumed 25.16M instructions across 1,001 visits in g3 and 6.54M across 899 visits in Z3. All these fresh children were Boolean. The term-ITE internalizer had zero visits in this group. Equality-specific theory notification consumed only 0.57M and 0.12M instructions respectively. Within the Boolean gates, recursive child work used 14.78M versus 4.03M and gate clauses and watches used about 8.0M versus 1.99M. The nested else child alone accounted for 12.63M versus 3.28M. The last figures overlap the recursive totals.

All 1,001 outer conditions in g3 already had a Boolean variable. Of those, 877 were true above the base level, 73 were false at a positive base level and 51 were unassigned. None had a permanent level-zero assignment. An encoding that omits a sibling branch based on the current value would need to restore its obligation on backtracking.

| Policy tested on the whole check | Reference, M instructions | Variant, M instructions |
|---|---:|---:|
| Lift arbitrary term conditionals into branch equalities | 887.2 | 1,080.7 |
| Normalize conditional Boolean equality to IFF | 887.3 | 1,067.8 |
| Distribute IFF into conditional branches | 887.3 | 1,196.4 |
| Split the conditional into two guarded clauses | 887.1 | 931.5 |
| Split only when the outer guard has an assignment, retaining both branches | 887.1 | 911.8 |

Each row uses the median of three rotating runs, with the ordinary policy in the same binary. All transcripts matched. None of these encodings earned a production change. The evidence favors examining what it costs to install the existing gate clauses and watches. The archive contains the overlay generators, counter data and whole-check trial results, including the exploratory one-branch controls. [Experiment archive](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-fresh-equality-conditionals.tar.xz)

### November 27 — Storage for scoped auxiliary clauses reduced to two literals

On TLB batch 60 check 1, storing each scoped, simplified binary clause together with its unit-resolution reason saved **5.86M solver-thread instructions (0.67%), 32,016 allocations (13.1%) and 85,536 allocated bytes**. The change applies to an ordinary auxiliary clause with two surviving literals, one removed false literal and no supplied justification or deletion handler. The reason retains the literal that explains the reduction. The clause still uses the ordinary watch, propagation, conflict and scope bookkeeping. [Clause and reason layout](smtcore/smt_clause.go) · [Eligibility and installation](smtcore/smt_internalizer.go) · [Regression and scope benchmark](smtcore/smt_resolved_clause_test.go)

| Measurement | Parent | Coallocated |
|---|---:|---:|
| TLB 60/1 instructions | 874,928,609 | 869,064,830 |
| TLB 60/1 allocations | 244,498 | 212,482 |
| TLB 60/1 allocated bytes | 25,818,600 | 25,733,064 |
| Push, insert 64 reduced clauses, pop | 22.08 µs | 17.64 µs |
| Allocations per 64-clause scope | 256 | 64 |
| Allocated bytes per 64-clause scope | 10,753 | 10,241 |

Each row uses seven samples per version. The whole-check comparison used alternating pinned runs with GC disabled. The scope benchmark used 3,000 operations per sample. With ordinary GC and five alternating pairs per complete workload, median paired instruction changes were +0.07% on TLB, −0.26% on POPL18 Ticket, −0.92% on ARM, +0.22% on nested Ticket, −0.80% on automatic Ticket and −0.21% on Raft no_assume. The whole-check saving is measurable even though the complete TLB run was effectively flat. Standard output, standard error and exit status matched the saved native references for 228 workloads and Apple rfn2 and dramc_nb2. [Drivers, per-run counters and transcript checks](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-scoped-binary-reasons.tar.xz)

**Where the cost came from.** Two reversed g3/Z3 pairs followed the 1,001/899 fresh Boolean ITEs immediately beneath positive equalities. Obtaining literals cost 1.12M/0.15M instructions, inserting four gate clauses cost 5.97M/1.60M and registering relevance watches cost 1.01M/0.34M. g3 stored 2,104 ordinary clauses, including 1,900 reduced binaries. Z3 stored 1,798, all reduced binaries. Neither solver introduced a unit assignment or conflict from the other gate clauses in this sample. On the reduced binaries alone, constructing the reason cost 1.09M/0.41M and creating the clause and linking its watches cost 1.72M/0.64M. Native appends the clause to its auxiliary list inside the latter interval. Per-phase hardware reads and logging perturb enclosing intervals. Use the uninstrumented whole-check comparison above to price the production change.

**What determined the layout.** Coallocating just the reason and one or two antecedent literals reduced allocations but raised the median bytes on the selected check by about 145 KB. Allocating just the clause and its attachment together saved about 17,000 allocations with effectively flat byte traffic. A solver-local span for reason literals reduced bytes but increased instructions on four complete workloads. An initial combined record with room for four retained literals also increased bytes. The retained layout uses three literal slots, with a two-element clause slice and a disjoint one-element reason slice. It requires one allocation where the ordinary path used four. Direct bound-literal lookup, reusing the condition's literal for both watches, a short-clause construction shortcut and blocks of sixteen clause records all produced mixed complete-workload results. The archive includes their trials. [Unit-resolution benchmark](smtcore/smt_unit_resolution_benchmark_test.go) · [Trial records](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-scoped-binary-reasons.tar.xz)

**Separate enode correction.** Z3 checks the original application's arity before marking an enode as an interpreted constant. Previously g3 tested the enode's argument count, which is zero whenever its arguments are suppressed. The regression showed that the compound datatype value `next(base)` was incorrectly marked alongside the nullary `base`. The fix uses the arity already read from the application and adds no field to the enode. Seven alternating TLB pairs measured 875.21M → 874.79M instructions. The semantic discrepancy independently warranted the correction. [Regression](smtcore/smt_enode_interpreted_test.go) · [Native implementation](../src/smt/smt_internalizer.cpp)

**Next source of recursive work.** After the coallocation change, g3 internalized 731 previously unbound negated OR operands on TLB 60/1 and Z3 internalized 518. Their child recursion used 10.09M and 2.26M instructions respectively. Two-input ORs alone accounted for 8.27M and 1.82M. An independent meter inside those two-input ORs found 100 fresh positive Boolean conditionals costing 4.71M instructions in g3, versus 76 costing 0.99M in Z3. Fresh negated OR children cost another 2.53M over 107 g3 visits, versus 0.58M over 86 native visits. Both the number of visits and the cost per visit matter here. These totals include recursive descendants, so do not add them to the parent totals. [Observer and raw data](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-scoped-binary-reasons.tar.xz)

Distributing a negated binary OR into two guarded clauses preserved all reference outputs and made the selected check more expensive. Three rotating whole-check runs measured 881.4M instructions for ordinary installation, 937.7M for unrestricted expansion, 937.4M for expansion only when the inner OR lacked a Boolean variable, 1086.0M when both children also had literals and 982.8M when at least one child lacked a literal. Every expansion installed both branches. Compare the quantifiers and bindings that produce the extra gates before trying another encoding.

### Matching the TLB quantifier installation stream

On TLB batch 60 check 1 at revision `afad63518`, g3 and linked Z3 created 731 and 518 fresh negated OR gates. We matched ten fresh symbols by their creating quantifier, binder and creation order. We then paired installations by quantified body, ordered ground bindings and occurrence. All 819 negated OR operands in 10,764 paired installations agreed structurally. Different prior Boolean binding state accounted for 15 extra fresh gates. The other 198 came from installations left unpaired, including extra repetitions of shared tuples.

The first different queue candidate was number 3,164. Replaying four bindings from the first differing model-based batch reproduced the native sequence of 12,605 installations, including every recorded negated OR and its binding status. Each single replacement increased instructions. All four together reduced the focal g3 check from 869M to 772M. A structural rule reused a binary counterexample’s first witness across trailing unary quantifiers when that witness belonged to their instantiation sets and falsified every affected body in the candidate model.

Across starting counters 407–414, the rule changed three histories, saving about 97M instructions at 407 and 37M each at 409 and 411. It left the expensive 413 history alone. All 230 complete reference transcripts matched in the broader eligibility survey. Only TLB changed bindings. With the instantiation-set requirement and ordinary GC, five alternating pairs on complete TLB gave −0.09% median instructions and −0.41% median wall time. Across the other five complete inputs the instruction changes ranged from −0.09% to +0.61%. Keep the rule in the benchmark archive. The evidence for enabling it across solvers is weak.

Holding the installation stream fixed exposes a larger implementation cost. In the first paired hardware-counter round g3 used 169.58M instructions internalizing 12,605 instances versus 55.92M in linked Z3. Rewriting those same instances used 121.95M versus 38.74M. Substitution cache misses numbered 5,077 in both and used 103.40M versus 41.79M. Profile internalization first using the matched stream, particularly the cost of already-bound literals and relevance work. The raw phase rows permit comparisons without attributing search differences to implementation. [Study drivers, raw measurements and replay](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-quantified-gate-origins.tar.xz)

### Signed watch registration on an identical quantifier stream

Linked Z3 and g3 performed the same 12,605 TLB installations in the matched witness replay. Two reversed-order pairs gave these median solver-thread instruction counts in millions. The component counters exclude their own logging.

| Installation operation | g3 before | g3 after | Z3 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Internalize operands and collect literals | 68.44 | 68.53 | 23.83 |
| Simplify and install the root clause | 25.28 | 25.35 | 9.84 |
| Register relevance watches | 32.29 | 24.17 | 9.74 |
| Mark the root and propagate relevance | 25.17 | 25.22 | 8.16 |

Commit `e18533cab` uses the signed SAT literal to read the current assignment and register the watch. Nested NOT, reserved constants and already-relevant parents keep the ordinary watch lookup. When an immediate callback detaches the propagator, later watches must observe the new assignment source. Removing the already-relevant guard made the regression panic. The retained change uses the existing trail and handler pool. Seven alternating pairs on the ordinary TLB search measured **869.13M → 859.71M instructions** for check 60/1. The four-literal registration and scope-pop benchmark fell from 379.5 to 303.7 ns with all four children unassigned, and from 280.5 to 215.3 ns with mixed assignments. [Callback regression](smtcore/smt_relevancy_asserted_or_test.go) · [Benchmark](smtcore/smt_root_relevance_benchmark_test.go)

Whole-process instruction changes were +0.01% on TLB, +0.17% on POPL18, +0.10% on ARM, +0.59% on nested Ticket, −1.71% on automatic Ticket and −0.27% on Raft no_assume. Three alternating pairs on complete Apple rfn2 and dramc_nb2 measured +0.61% and +0.13% respectively. These comparisons establish a local reduction in registration work. They do not establish a general end-to-end elapsed speedup. All 230 complete transcripts and exit codes matched native references.

The largest per-installation cost is still collecting operands. Four rotating whole-check experiments on the parent measured 868.95M instructions for baseline, 865.48M when recursion skipped already-bound gate children, 868.35M for reading retained gate arguments, and 864.93M together. The combined saving of 0.46% does little to close the gap. Both prototypes stay in the archive. [Benchmark drivers, raw counters and verification results](perf/ivy_apple/holdouts/nov27-matched-watch-installation.tar.xz)

The combined preparation column includes asserting the base, initializing the verification batch, trying early proofs, and the first concrete push in each batch. It measures those operations together even when early proofs save a native check. Values are g3 minus linked Z3 in millions of solver-thread instructions. The total covers the instrumented stages and excludes the rest of the frontend.

| Complete input | Base assertion | First push | Combined preparation | Concrete checks | All measured stages |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

On Hybrid, charging just the first push to preprocessing overstates the net preparation deficit by about 649M. ## ARM and automatic Ticket across seven expensive checks

All seven checks ran after their real incremental history. Three rotations measured retired user instructions on the solver thread, with GC disabled for the phase comparison. One run measured the whole check and another enabled counters around candidate satisfaction, substitution, rewriting, and installation. Subtracting those four intervals leaves the “outside” estimate. The numbers below are millions of instructions, g3 / linked Z3. Candidate and installation counts are event counts. The previous ordinary-GC stage study and this GC-disabled experiment measure different costs.

| Check | Whole | Outside the four operations | Candidates | Installations |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ARM 6/4 | 103.09 / 39.36 | 87.61 / 33.30 | 1,127 / 1,127 | 284 / 284 |
| ARM 6/5 | 190.33 / 77.08 | 144.92 / 59.70 | 2,704 / 2,704 | 720 / 720 |
| ARM 6/6 | 175.65 / 67.05 | 129.99 / 50.53 | 2,201 / 2,201 | 646 / 646 |
| Ticket 12/8 | 176.92 / 93.08 | 76.59 / 43.34 | 7,821 / 8,454 | 1,983 / 2,490 |
| Ticket 13/8 | 88.42 / 40.43 | 40.50 / 19.73 | 3,618 / 3,978 | 861 / 861 |
| Ticket 14/8 | 101.25 / 38.67 | 42.25 / 17.89 | 3,619 / 3,127 | 1,087 / 908 |
| Ticket 16/1 | 97.75 / 45.69 | 38.70 / 23.85 | 2,330 / 2,158 | 958 / 942 |

Identical aggregate candidate and installation counts on ARM leave 219M of the 286M excess instructions outside the four measured operations. Three hardware sampling profiles per solver and check put ARM equality merging at roughly 58M / 20.5M, conflict resolution at 67M / 34.5M and relevance notification at 20M / 4.5M. Inclusive stack estimates overlap. On Ticket 12/8, g3 installed 507 fewer lemmas and still spent 34.35M / 14.48M rewriting and 34.49M / 12.84M installing. Faster routine work can help even where native executes more instances.

Reusing a declaration ID during matcher notification and sharing the validated expression header between relevance consumers saved 6.9M instructions across the three ARM checks and 2.4M across the four Ticket checks. Five alternating pairs with ordinary GC gave median paired reductions of 1.21% on complete ARM and 0.59% on automatic Ticket. Neither Apple isolate moved by 0.1% in three paired runs. The release at `b79866e51` matched all 230 native transcripts and exit statuses.

An exact-key home-slot shortcut for congruence erasure saved 6.3M instructions on the selected ARM checks. The miss microbenchmark took 9.9% more instructions and the commuted erasure took 2.8% more. A variant that waited for the normal probe to find the ordered slot saved less on ARM. Both remain experiments. A future fast path could be restricted to caller sites that already know the representative.

The heap profiles identify different pressures on the two workloads. ARM allocated 646,848 bytes for 3,369 CHECK instructions alone. On Ticket the two largest solver allocation sites were enodes (1.40 MB) and fingerprints (1.22 MB). The allocation snapshots used `memprofilerate=1` and forced collections outside the target check. Separate runs used ordinary GC and `runtime.ReadMemStats` immediately outside the measured interval. Allocation profiles serve to identify sites, while the latter runs measure the change in total bytes.

### Compact matcher instructions

The C++ matcher uses opcode-specific instruction structs. The Go interpreter previously allocated a single 192-byte record even for CHECK, which needs a register and an enode. Splitting application and yield operands from the common record reduces CHECK and INIT to 80 allocated bytes each on amd64. The extended records own their operands in the same allocation. No shared mutable allocator or unsafe conversion is needed.

Six rotating rounds with ordinary GC reduced total allocation across the three ARM checks from 6,792,400 to 5,990,424 bytes (11.8%). Automatic Ticket changed from 10,984,720 to 10,946,832 bytes (0.34%). With GC off, the ARM checks used 455.95M / 455.10M instructions before / after and Ticket used 445.28M / 445.59M. In five alternating pairs on six complete verifiers, the median paired instruction changes ranged from −0.29% to +0.16%. All 230 native references matched. Keep the split for its measured memory saving. Storing up to three binding indexes inline reduced allocation counts on ARM but allocated more bytes than the simpler split on both workloads.

### A 48-byte allocation for each recursively internalized formula child

The production PGO profile inlined `Internalize` into the formula child loop. Escape analysis reported that the validated AST header moved to the heap at that call site. A build without the profile missed the escape. Passing the header by value into `internalizeFormulaCoreOp` preserves the arena and the normal inlining decisions. The PGO benchmark rebuilds a scoped OR over already internalized children. At width 2 it went from 496 to 400 B/op and from 11 to 9 allocations. At width 32 it went from 5,512 to 3,976 B/op and from 102 to 70 allocations. The 32-child median fell from 13.84 to 12.53 µs over six alternating pairs.

The isolated change recovered about 7,348 allocations across the ARM checks and 13,392 across the Ticket checks, saving 353 KB and 643 KB. Independently disabling inlining on the entire entry point recovered the same bytes. With GC disabled the value change saved 1.01M ARM and 1.48M Ticket instructions across the selected checks. Applied after the compact matcher, it reduced median paired instructions on all six complete verifiers by 0.11–0.39%. All 230 native references matched. Comparing both changes together with the notification release, dramc_nb2 instructions changed by +0.10% in three pairs. The first three rfn2 pairs showed +0.26% instructions and +8.8% elapsed, with substantial run-to-run timing variation. Nine further rfn2 pairs gave −0.10% instructions and +0.57% elapsed. These runs establish an allocation saving. They give no evidence of an Apple elapsed-time win.

### Where the conflict-resolution samples went

Separating the immediate callees of the conflict resolver puts 50.0M / 27.5M sampled ARM instructions in scope pop, and 39.5M / 11.0M on automatic Ticket. Scope pop accounts for most of the sampled resolver gap on each. On Ticket, 29 g3 samples (about 14.5M instructions) reached the relevance propagator directly from the inner pop routine. Congruence erase and insert together accounted for seven such samples. ARM showed the opposite weighting with 37 congruence erase/insert samples and 18 relevance pop samples. Sample counts are coarse, and compiler inlining affects frame boundaries. The earlier counts already matched the number of conflict resolutions on ARM 6/5 and 6/6. The next experiment should time the separate unmark, AST-reference release and watch-unlink phases on Ticket during backjump, alongside the corresponding native pop. [Earlier matched operations](#november-27--search-volume-and-cost-per-merge-in-live-arm)

## Automatic Ticket relevance restoration during backjump

Four checks in their original incremental histories (12/8, 13/8, 14/8 and 16/1) ran with the production g3 PGO profile and linked Z3. Five alternating rounds measured solver-thread user instructions with GC disabled. Each timed block subtracted an adjacent empty counter read. All stdout, stderr and exit statuses matched the native reference. The counters include every relevance pop in the selected checks. A separate stack profile identifies the pops under conflict resolution.

| Operation | g3 entries | Z3 entries | g3 instructions | Z3 instructions |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Unmark relevant expressions | 14,051 | 14,568 | 1.13M | 0.80M |
| Release the marked-expression suffix | 14,051 | 14,568 | 2.31M | 1.33M |
| Undo watch and handler registrations | 10,415 | 11,293 | 8.18M | 0.98M |

g3 made 137 pops and Z3 made 200. The 7.20M excess in registration undo includes destroying ASTs. An independent observer identified **3,144 final releases of asserted parent expressions** from g3's watch trail, costing 6.00M instructions. All 10,415 watch-source decrements left the source alive. Z3 kept its parents in the marked-expression vector, and all 11,293 native watch-source decrements also left their source alive.

Counting both owners, g3 made 4,692 final decrements (3,144 parents plus 1,548 marked expressions), versus 4,963 in native. These consumed 8.01M / 1.26M instructions, or about 1,707 / 255 per final decrement. This is an aggregate of different search histories and term shapes. The mark observer releases one element at a time in original order. Its per-element cost for surviving references includes the extra call and should not be summed with the independently timed bulk intervals.

The combined excess in all three pop operations is 8.50M instructions. Earlier measurements of these same four checks put the whole-check excess near 246M and the excess in quantifier rewriting and installation near 123M. Even eliminating the entire pop difference would recover only about 3.5% of the check gap. The older matched-arity experiment found a sevenfold final-release cost on a different Ticket workload; its wide-operand shortcut regressed on complete proofs. Skipping declaration metadata lookups for other node kinds in the current worklist saved only 0.14M instructions on automatic Ticket and was flat on ARM. Keep that change as an experiment. [Earlier destruction experiments](#november-27--wide-ast-deletion-and-the-complete-verifier-release-decision)

### Retiring watch links in trail order

The three relevance tables each allocated a free list even though the shared trail always removes the newest registration in its table. A callback walking the list reads its next index and handler before invoking user code. The retained change uses a count of live links in the existing solver-local pages. Pop restores the previous head and decrements the count. Refused reference releases still retry separately after unlinking.

| Layout | 128 surviving watches, pop only | Fresh table, 4,096 registrations and pops | Allocated bytes per fresh table at 4,096 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Existing free list | 1,999 ns | 67.78 µs | 50,552 |
| Reverse-order pages | 1,462 ns | 52.15 µs | 50,552 |
| Growing slice | 1,395 ns | 60.15 µs | 162,936 |

The watch-pop column uses the median of nine rotations, with registrations outside the timer. Fresh-table measurements use six rotations and include allocation. One registration took 1,168 bytes in the slice versus 4,232 in the paged table. At 4,096 registrations slice growth more than tripled the bytes allocated. All layouts produced the same registration order. [Fresh-table benchmark](smtcore/smt_relevancy_link_storage_benchmark_test.go)

On automatic Ticket the paged change saved 0.42% of complete-verifier instructions in five pairs and 0.78% in a separate twelve-round, three-layout rotation. The latter recorded 1.12% higher median paired elapsed time. ARM and nested Ticket moved by less than 0.3% in instructions in both paged comparisons. The first panel recorded 0.74% more instructions on POPL18 Ticket. Keep the page-backed version for the measured reduction in watch work and predictable storage at higher widths. No overall elapsed speedup is established. Commit `ae1a382d8` passed the smtcore and api suites, checked/debug/trace scope and relevancy tests, vet, and all 230 native reference transcripts.

### Which theory reductions account for automatic Ticket rewriting?

Six gated stack profiles per goal and engine pointed to application traversal and theory reduction. A separate pair of instrumented verifiers timed the call to `reduce_app_core` and its Go equivalent only while the quantifier queue rewrote an instance. Three alternating rounds reproduced every reference outcome and every per-operator call count. The grouping includes batch, goal, declaration family, operator, arity and return status. Matching the smaller call count in each group and multiplying by the difference in per-call costs estimates the effect of cost per reduction. Nodes within a group can still have different operands.

| Core reduction result | g3 calls | Z3 calls | g3 instructions | Z3 instructions |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Equality, no rule applied | 2,520 | 2,754 | 4.81M | 0.58M |
| OR, no rule applied | 6,071 | 6,531 | 5.45M | 2.53M |
| OR, produced a result | 882 | 885 | 3.61M | 0.95M |
| NOT, no rule applied | 6,507 | 6,845 | 3.13M | 0.59M |
| All operator/status groups | 23,800 | 36,414 | 18.96M | 4.86M |

The differences in per-call cost explain 13.71M of the 14.10M excess inside core reduction under this grouping. Although failed equality is expensive (about 1,908 / 211 instructions per call), its entire excess is 4.23M. The independently measured excess for the whole queue rewrite on these inputs is 60.02M. Most of that difference falls outside core reduction. A single lookup for both declaration family and kind saved 1.41M on the four Ticket checks and 0.86M on the three ARM checks with GC off. Complete automatic Ticket changed by −0.05% and ARM by +0.65% in the five-pair panel. Keep this as a measured prototype.

A larger next experiment is to match application frames by operator, arity and child-change status, counting frame entries, child visits and cache hits within each queued instance. Split time outside core reduction between visiting operands and finishing unchanged frames, including result references and cache insertion. Compare with native on the same groups. This tests whether g3 traverses more terms or spends more per visit before investing in another individual Boolean rule.
